conversations.title: Opening up about feeling burned out
conversations.situation: You text a close friend late at night to admit you've been feeling overwhelmed and stressed about everything lately.
conversations.tip: When you're the one venting, friends respond best to short honest lines; let them react and 되묻기 (왜?/무슨 일인데?) instead of dumping everything at once.

turns.ko: 자?
turns.romanization: ja?
turns.en: You asleep?

turns.prompt: Say you're up and admit you can't sleep.

choices.ko: 아니 안 자 ㅋㅋ 요즘 잠이 안 와
choices.romanization: ani an ja kk yojeum jami an wa
choices.en: Nope, still up lol I can't really sleep these days
choices.feedback: Casual 아니 안 자 plus a small honest hint opens the door for them to ask more.

choices.en: I have not yet gone to bed. (formal)
choices.feedback: 취침 전입니다 is stiff 존댓말 — nobody texts a close friend like this.

choices.en: Yeah, goodnight.
choices.feedback: Shuts the chat down right when they were checking in on you.

turns.ko: 왜? 무슨 일 있어? 너 요즘 좀 다운돼 보이더라
turns.romanization: wae? museun il isseo? neo yojeum jom daundwae boideora
turns.en: Why, is something up? You've seemed kind of down lately.

turns.prompt: Admit you're overwhelmed without over-explaining.

choices.ko: 그냥 좀… 요즘 다 벅차 ㅠㅠ 번아웃 온 거 같아
choices.romanization: geunyang jom… yojeum da beokcha yuyu beonaut on geo gata
choices.en: Just kinda… everything feels like too much lately ㅠㅠ I think I'm burned out
choices.feedback: Honest but short — 다 벅차 + 번아웃 is exactly how 20-30s name this feeling, and it invites them in.

choices.en: A considerable amount of psychological pressure has accumulated. (formal)
choices.feedback: Reads like a report — way too clinical and formal for venting to a friend.

choices.ko: 아니야 별일 아니야 신경 쓰지 마.
choices.romanization: aniya byeoril aniya singyeong sseuji ma.
choices.en: No it's nothing, don't worry about it.
choices.feedback: Brushes them off and closes up — defeats the point of opening the chat.

turns.ko: 헐… 그랬구나 ㅠㅠ 혼자 끙끙 앓지 말고 진작 말하지 그랬어
turns.romanization: heol… geuraetguna yuyu honja kkeungkkeung alchi malgo jinjang malhaji geuraesseo
turns.en: Oh no… I had no idea ㅠㅠ You should've told me sooner instead of bottling it up alone.

turns.prompt: Thank them and admit it's hard to say out loud.

choices.ko: ㅠㅠ 고마워 막상 말하려니까 좀 그렇더라
choices.romanization: yuyu gomawo maksang malharyeonikka jom geureoteora
choices.en: ㅠㅠ thanks, it's just kinda hard to actually say it out loud
choices.feedback: Warm and real — 막상 말하려니까 그렇더라 is a very natural way to admit it's awkward to open up.

choices.en: I sincerely thank you for listening. (formal)
choices.feedback: 감사드립니다 is business-letter formal — kills the intimate moment.

choices.en: Anyway what are you doing this weekend?
choices.feedback: Abruptly changes the subject right when they're being caring.

turns.ko: 야 우리 내일 만나서 얘기하자 내가 맛있는 거 사줄게
turns.romanization: ya uri naeil mannaseo yaegihaja naega masinneun geo sajulge
turns.en: Hey let's meet tomorrow and talk, I'll buy you something tasty

turns.prompt: Accept gratefully and show it means a lot.

choices.ko: 헐 진짜? ㅠㅠ 너 덕분에 좀 살 거 같다 고마워
choices.romanization: heol jinjja? yuyu neo deokbune jom sal geo gatda gomawo
choices.en: Wait really? ㅠㅠ honestly you're kind of saving me here, thank you
choices.feedback: 헐 진짜? + 너 덕분에 살 거 같다 is heartfelt and casual (use 덕분에, not 때문에, when you're grateful) — the perfect close to a vent.

choices.ko: 그럼 내일 일정을 조율해 보도록 하겠습니다.
choices.romanization: geureom naeil iljeongeul joyulhae bodoro kagetseumnida.
choices.en: Then I shall coordinate my schedule for tomorrow. (formal)
choices.feedback: Sounds like scheduling a work meeting — totally wrong register for a friend.

choices.ko: 아니야 안 사줘도 돼 그냥 둬.
choices.romanization: aniya an sajwodo dwae geunyang dwo.
choices.en: No you don't have to buy anything, just leave it.
choices.feedback: Reflexively refusing the kindness shuts down their warm offer.

buddyCard.instructionKo: 늦은 밤에 연락을 받은 친한 친구 역할을 해 주세요. 학습자는 초급이에요. 천천히 잠이 안 오는지 묻고, 요즘 무슨 일로 힘든지도 물어봐 주세요.

conversations.title: Comforting a friend having a rough time
conversations.situation: A friend texts you out of nowhere saying they're going through a really rough patch and feel like everything's falling apart.
conversations.tip: When comforting someone, validate the feeling first (얼마나 힘들어/그럴 만하지) and avoid jumping to solutions — let 맞장구 and gentle 되묻기 do the work.

turns.ko: 나 요즘 진짜 다 무너지는 기분이야 ㅠㅠ
turns.romanization: na yojeum jinjja da muneojineun gibuniya yuyu
turns.en: Lately I genuinely feel like everything's falling apart ㅠㅠ

turns.prompt: Validate first and gently ask what's going on.

choices.ko: 헐… 무슨 일이야? 많이 힘들었구나 ㅠㅠ
choices.romanization: heol… museun iriya? mani himdeureotguna yuyu
choices.en: Oh no… what's going on? you've been having such a hard time ㅠㅠ
choices.feedback: Validates the feeling (많이 힘들었구나) before asking — exactly what someone hurting needs first.

choices.en: Could you explain the specific situation? (formal)
choices.feedback: 설명해 주시겠어요 is cold 존댓말 — sounds like a survey, not a friend.

choices.ko: 야 그래도 너보다 힘든 사람 많아.
choices.romanization: ya geuraedo neoboda himdeun saram mana.
choices.en: Hey, still, there are people way worse off than you.
choices.feedback: Minimizes their pain — the opposite of comforting.

turns.ko: 일도 꼬이고 사람한테도 상처받고… 그냥 다 놓고 싶어
turns.romanization: ildo kkoigo saramhantedo sangcheobatgo… geunyang da noko sipeo
turns.en: Work's a mess and people hurt me too… I just wanna let it all go

turns.prompt: Acknowledge how heavy that is without fixing it.

choices.ko: 그럴 만하지… 한꺼번에 몰리면 진짜 버겁잖아
choices.romanization: geureol manhaji… hankkeobeone mollimyeon jinjja beogeopjana
choices.en: No wonder… when it all piles up at once it's genuinely too much
choices.feedback: 그럴 만하지 normalizes the feeling and 버겁잖아 shows you really get it — pure comfort, no lecture.

choices.en: At times like these you must think positively. (formal)
choices.feedback: A 존댓말 pep-talk lecture — invalidating and the last thing they want to hear.

choices.ko: 그래서 그 사람이 정확히 뭐라고 했는데?
choices.romanization: geuraeseo geu sarami jeonghwaki mworago haenneunde?
choices.en: So what exactly did that person say to you?
choices.feedback: Digs for gossip details instead of sitting with their feelings.

turns.ko: 응 ㅠㅠ 요즘 그냥 아무것도 하기 싫고 무기력해
turns.romanization: eung yuyu yojeum geunyang amugeotdo hagi silko mugiryeokae
turns.en: Yeah ㅠㅠ lately I just don't wanna do anything, I feel so drained

turns.prompt: Reassure them it's okay to rest right now.

choices.ko: 그럴 땐 좀 쉬어도 돼 진짜. 너 충분히 잘하고 있어
choices.romanization: geureol ttaen jom swieodo dwae jinjja. neo chungbunhi jalhago isseo
choices.en: It's totally okay to rest when you feel like that. you're doing more than enough
choices.feedback: Permission to rest + 충분히 잘하고 있어 is warm, affirming comfort — exactly right.

choices.en: For lethargy, professional counseling is recommended. (formal)
choices.feedback: Robotic 존댓말 advice — reads like a pamphlet, not a friend who cares.

choices.ko: 에이 그러다 진짜 큰일 나, 정신 차려.
choices.romanization: ei geureoda jinjja keunil na, jeongsin charyeo.
choices.en: Come on, keep that up and you're in real trouble, snap out of it.
choices.feedback: Scolding tone — pressures them instead of comforting them.

turns.ko: 고마워 ㅠㅠ 진짜 네 말 들으니까 좀 위로된다
turns.romanization: gomawo yuyu jinjja ne mal deureunikka jom wirodoenda
turns.en: Thank you ㅠㅠ hearing you say that actually comforts me

turns.prompt: Let them know you're always there for them.

choices.ko: 언제든 연락해 진짜. 나 항상 네 편이야
choices.romanization: eonjedeun yeollakae jinjja. na hangsang ne pyeoniya
choices.en: Reach out anytime, I mean it. I'm always on your side
choices.feedback: 나 항상 네 편이야 is the perfect close — open, warm, and reassuring.

choices.en: I'm glad to hear I was of help. (formal)
choices.feedback: 다행스럽게 생각합니다 is stiff 존댓말 — too businesslike for a heart-to-heart.

choices.en: Okay then, I'm gonna head to bed now.
choices.feedback: Bailing the moment they open up feels cold and abrupt.

buddyCard.instructionKo: 요즘 여러 일로 지친 친한 친구 역할을 해 주세요. 학습자는 초급이에요. 천천히 힘든 마음을 이야기하고, 잠깐 이야기를 들어 줄 수 있는지 물어봐 주세요.
buddyCard.reactionKo: 고마워, 네 말 들으니까 좀 위로된다.

conversations.title: Ranting about an annoying roommate
conversations.situation: You're hanging out at a cafe and your friend starts ranting about their messy, inconsiderate roommate.
conversations.tip: For a 'this is so annoying' rant, your job is to be on their side — pile on with 맞장구 (헐/대박/그니까) and 되묻기 (그래서 뭐래?) so they feel backed up.

turns.ko: 아 진짜 나 룸메 때문에 미치겠어
turns.romanization: a jinjja na rumme ttaemune michigesseo
turns.en: Ugh seriously my roommate is driving me insane

turns.prompt: Take their side and ask what happened this time.

choices.ko: 헐 또 왜? 무슨 일인데 ㅋㅋ
choices.romanization: heol tto wae? museun irinde kk
choices.en: Ugh what now? what happened lol
choices.feedback: 헐 또 왜? immediately takes their side and pulls the story out — perfect rant fuel.

choices.en: Are you having a conflict with your roommate? (formal)
choices.feedback: 갈등이 있으신가요 is 존댓말 — absurdly formal when you're sitting right across from them.

choices.ko: 룸메랑 같이 사는 거 원래 힘들어.
choices.romanization: rummerang gachi saneun geo wollae himdeureo.
choices.en: Living with a roommate is hard in general.
choices.feedback: A flat generalization that doesn't react or invite the story.

turns.ko: 설거지를 일주일째 안 해 ㅋㅋㅋ 싱크대에 그릇이 산더미야
turns.romanization: seolgeojireul iljuiljjae an hae kkk singkeudaee geureusi sandeomiya
turns.en: They haven't done dishes in a week lol the sink is a literal mountain of plates

turns.prompt: React big and pile on.

choices.ko: 헐 대박 ㅋㅋㅋ 일주일?? 그걸 어떻게 참아
choices.romanization: heol daebak kkk iljuil?? geugeol eotteoke chama
choices.en: Whoa no way lol a whole week?? how do you even put up with that
choices.feedback: Big reaction (대박) + 그걸 어떻게 참아 backs them up and keeps the rant rolling.

choices.ko: 위생상 좋지 않으니 즉시 처리해야 합니다.
choices.romanization: wisaengsang jochi aneuni jeuksi cheorihaeya hamnida.
choices.en: It's unhygienic so it should be dealt with immediately. (formal)
choices.feedback: A hygiene lecture in 존댓말 — kills the vibe and sides with no one.

choices.en: Do you tend to do your dishes right away?
choices.feedback: Flips the focus onto you instead of backing them up.

turns.ko: 그러게 ㅋㅋ 어제는 한마디 했더니 알겠다고만 하고 또 안 함
turns.romanization: geureoge kk eojeneun hanmadi haetdeoni algetdagoman hago tto an ham
turns.en: Right lol yesterday I said something and they just went 'okay' and still didn't do it

turns.prompt: Share their frustration and dig for more.

choices.ko: 와 그게 더 빡치지 ㅋㅋ 그래서 너 뭐라고 했어?
choices.romanization: wa geuge deo ppakchiji kk geuraeseo neo mworago haesseo?
choices.en: Ugh that's even more infuriating lol so what did you say to them?
choices.feedback: 그게 더 빡치지 matches their anger and 그래서 뭐라고 했어? keeps the story going.

choices.en: I recommend resolving it through amicable conversation. (formal)
choices.feedback: Sounds like an HR memo — formal and preachy, not what a ranting friend wants.

choices.ko: 근데 우리 뭐 마실지 안 정했다.
choices.romanization: geunde uri mwo masilji an jeonghaetda.
choices.en: Anyway we still haven't decided what to drink.
choices.feedback: Changes the subject mid-rant — leaves them hanging.

turns.ko: 그냥 포기했어 ㅋㅋㅋ 결국 내가 치워야지 뭐
turns.romanization: geunyang pogihaesseo kkk gyeolgung naega chiwoyaji mwo
turns.en: I just gave up lol I guess I'll have to clean it myself in the end.

turns.prompt: Sympathize and lightly side with them.

choices.ko: 에휴 고생이다 진짜 ㅋㅋ 넌 너무 착하다
choices.romanization: ehyu gosaengida jinjja kk neon neomu chakada
choices.en: Aw what a pain seriously lol you're way too nice
choices.feedback: 고생이다 + 넌 너무 착하다 (the -다 exclamatory ending is super natural here) sympathizes and subtly takes their side — a natural rant wrap-up.

choices.ko: 갈등 해결을 위해 규칙을 정립하시는 게 어떨까요?
choices.romanization: galdeung haegyeoreul wihae gyuchigeul jeongnipasineun ge eotteolkkayo?
choices.en: How about establishing rules to resolve the conflict? (formal)
choices.feedback: 규칙을 정립하시는 is stiff 존댓말 — overly solution-y for a casual vent.

choices.ko: 그러게 왜 그런 애랑 같이 살아.
choices.romanization: geureoge wae geureon aerang gachi sara.
choices.en: Yeah well, why even live with someone like that.
choices.feedback: Blames them for the situation instead of being on their side.

buddyCard.instructionKo: 룸메이트 때문에 답답한 친한 친구 역할을 해 주세요. 학습자는 초급이에요. 최근에 있었던 일을 천천히 말하고, 학습자는 어떻게 생각하는지 물어봐 주세요.
buddyCard.reactionKo: 그치? 나 진짜 너무 답답해 ㅋㅋ

conversations.title: Asking to push the plan
conversations.situation: You're too wiped out for tomorrow's plan, so you text a friend to push it to next week.
conversations.tip: When you bail, soften it: a quick 미안 + a reason + offering a new day keeps it casual and not flaky. Tossing back 언제가 좋아? hands them the choice.

turns.ko: 내일 몇 시에 볼까?
turns.romanization: naeil myeot sie bolkka?
turns.en: What time should we meet tomorrow?

turns.prompt: Apologize and ask to push it to next week.

choices.ko: 아 미안ㅠ 나 내일 말고 담주에 보면 안 될까?
choices.romanization: a mianyu na naeil malgo damjue bomyeon an doelkka?
choices.en: Ah sorry ㅠ could we do next week instead of tomorrow?
choices.feedback: 미안 + 담주 (next week) + a soft 안 될까? is exactly how friends ask to reschedule.

choices.en: I'm sorry but I would like to change our appointment.
choices.feedback: Way too formal — 죄송하지만/변경하다 sounds like a business email, not a friend.

choices.en: What time should we meet tomorrow?
choices.feedback: That just repeats their question instead of asking to move the plan.

turns.ko: 오 그래 괜찮아~ 무슨 일 있어?
turns.romanization: o geurae gwaenchana~ museun il isseo?
turns.en: Oh sure, no problem~ is something up?

turns.prompt: Say you're just exhausted lately.

choices.en: No, I've just been so tired lately ㅠㅠ
choices.feedback: 그냥 + a real reason is natural and honest — friends don't need a big excuse.

choices.en: There is no particular reason.
choices.feedback: 사유/없습니다 is stiff bureaucratic Korean — friends say 그냥.

choices.en: Is something up with you lately?
choices.feedback: Flips the question back at them instead of answering — doesn't fit.

turns.ko: 헐 푹 쉬어ㅠ 그럼 담주 언제가 좋아?
turns.romanization: heol puk swieoyu geureom damju eonjega joa?
turns.en: Aw get some rest ㅠ so when next week works for you?

turns.prompt: Suggest the weekend and bounce it back.

choices.en: How about the weekend? Saturday or Sunday!
choices.feedback: A concrete option (토욜/일욜) plus 어때? keeps the rescheduling moving.

choices.en: I am available on the weekend.
choices.feedback: 가능합니다 is too formal — with a friend just say 주말 어때?

choices.en: Yeah I'll rest well, thanks.
choices.feedback: Polite, but it drops the ball — they asked which day, so you should pick one.

turns.ko: 콜! 토욜로 하자 ㅎㅎ
turns.romanization: kol! toyollo haja hh
turns.en: Deal! Let's do Saturday hehe

turns.prompt: Confirm and thank them for understanding.

choices.en: Okay, Saturday! Thanks for understanding hehe
choices.feedback: 오키 + confirming the day + a quick thanks is a warm, natural sign-off.

choices.en: Thank you for your understanding (formal).
choices.feedback: 양해/감사합니다 is customer-service formal — too stiff for a friend.

choices.en: Saturday's kind of iffy.
choices.feedback: Contradicts what you both just agreed on — confusing.

buddyCard.instructionKo: 내일 만나기로 한 친한 친구 역할을 해 주세요. 학습자는 초급이에요. 몇 시에 만날지 묻고, 약속을 미루면 다음 주 언제가 좋은지도 천천히 물어봐 주세요.

conversations.title: Warning you'll be late
conversations.situation: You're stuck and running about 20 minutes late, so you text the friend already waiting.
conversations.tip: Give a heads-up early with a time (한 20분), a reason, and what they should do meanwhile (먼저 들어가 있어). 미안 ㅠ goes a long way.

turns.ko: 야 너 어디야? 나 도착했어
turns.romanization: ya neo eodiya? na dochakaesseo
turns.en: Hey, where are you? I'm here.

turns.prompt: Warn them you'll be about 20 min late and say sorry.

choices.ko: 헉 미안ㅠ 나 한 20분 늦을 거 같아
choices.romanization: heong mianyu na han 20bun neujeul geo gata
choices.en: Oh no, sorry ㅠ I think I'll be about 20 min late
choices.feedback: Heads-up with a number (한 20분) + 미안 is exactly the right move when you're running late.

choices.en: My arrival is expected to be delayed.
choices.feedback: 지연/예정입니다 reads like a train announcement — friends say 늦을 거 같아.

choices.en: Where are you?
choices.feedback: Just echoes their question — doesn't tell them you're late.

turns.ko: 헐 왜? 무슨 일 있어?
turns.romanization: heol wae? museun il isseo?
turns.en: What, why? Did something happen?

turns.prompt: Explain the bus is super late.

choices.en: The bus isn't coming ㅠ I'm seriously losing it
choices.feedback: A real, vivid reason + 미치겠다 sounds like a frustrated friend in the moment.

choices.en: I am late due to public transit circumstances.
choices.feedback: 사정으로 인하여 is formal/written — nobody texts a friend like this.

choices.en: Yeah, did something happen?
choices.feedback: Bounces the question back instead of explaining why you're late.

turns.ko: 아 괜찮아ㅋㅋ 천천히 와~
turns.romanization: a gwaenchanakk cheoncheonhi wa~
turns.en: Ah it's fine lol take your time~

turns.prompt: Tell them to go in first and order without you.

choices.ko: ㅇㅇ 먼저 들어가 있어! 음료 먼저 시켜 놔ㅋㅋ
choices.romanization: ngng meonjeo deureoga isseo! eumnyo meonjeo sikyeo nwakk
choices.en: Yeah, go in first and order a drink while you wait lol
choices.feedback: 먼저 들어가 있어 + 음료 먼저 시켜 놔 naturally gives your waiting friend something to do.

choices.en: Please enter ahead of me (formal).
choices.feedback: 입장/바랍니다 is announcement-speak — say 먼저 들어가 있어.

choices.en: How's the vibe at that cafe?
choices.feedback: Random subject change — doesn't deal with you being late.

turns.ko: ㅇㅋㅋㅋ 알겠어 빨리 와
turns.romanization: ngkkk algesseo ppalli wa
turns.en: Okay lol got it, hurry up

turns.prompt: Say you're almost there and apologize again.

choices.ko: 거의 다 왔어! 금방 갈게 미안ㅠ
choices.romanization: geoui da wasseo! geumbang galge mianyu
choices.en: Almost there! I'll be quick, sorry ㅠ

conversations.situation: You feel sick the day of the plan and text a friend to cancel and do it another time.

turns.ko: 오늘 저녁에 보는 거 맞지?

turns.en: We're still on for tonight, right?

turns.prompt: Say you're not feeling great and ask to do it another time.

choices.ko: 미안ㅠ 나 오늘 컨디션이 너무 안 좋아서 다음에 보면 안 될까?

choices.feedback: 컨디션이 안 좋아 + 다음에 + 안 될까? is the standard, kind way to cancel and reschedule.

choices.feedback: 금일/난조/취소합니다 is formal written Korean — robotic for a friend.

choices.en: We're still on for tonight, right?
choices.feedback: Just repeats their line instead of canceling.

choices.en: Forget the meds, I'll just sleep.

choices.en: I'm already all better lol

choices.feedback: Just mirrors them with no offer or plan — the chat stalls.

choices.ko: 베이킹의 치유 효과에 대해 동의하는 바입니다.
choices.romanization: beikingui chiyu hyogwae daehae donguihaneun baimnida.
choices.en: I concur regarding the therapeutic effects of baking.
choices.feedback: Absurdly formal for chatting face to face with a friend.

choices.en: So when are you giving me bread?
choices.feedback: Jumps to demanding bread — it shifts focus off their story too soon and feels self-centered.

turns.ko: 한두 달? 처음엔 진짜 다 망했는데 요즘 좀 늘었어
turns.romanization: handu dal? cheoeumen jinjja da manghaenneunde yojeum jom neureosseo
turns.en: Like two months? At first everything flopped, but I've gotten better lately.

turns.prompt: Encourage and ask what they made recently

choices.en: That's awesome, I'm jealous — what'd you make recently?
choices.feedback: Warm hype (대박/부럽다) plus a follow-up — perfect for keeping a friend sharing.

choices.en: I presume it is the result of continuous effort.
choices.feedback: Reads like a written report — no one talks to a friend like this.

choices.en: Two months means you're still a beginner, huh.
choices.feedback: Slightly dismissive — it deflates their progress instead of cheering them on.

turns.ko: 지난주에 휘낭시에 구웠는데 그건 좀 성공했어 ㅋㅋ
turns.romanization: jinanjue hwinangsie guwonneunde geugeon jom seonggonghaesseo kk
turns.en: I baked financiers last week and those actually turned out lol

turns.prompt: Hint that you want to try one

choices.ko: 오, 휘낭시에 ㅋㅋ 다음에 나도 하나 맛봐도 돼?
choices.romanization: o, hwinangsie kk daeume nado hana matbwado dwae?
choices.en: Oh, financiers lol. Can I try one next time?
choices.feedback: Playful and hints at next time — a natural, friendly way to wrap while leaving the door open.

choices.ko: 다음 기회에 시식할 수 있도록 부탁드립니다.
choices.romanization: daeum gihoee sisikal su itdorok butakdeurimnida.
choices.en: I request the opportunity to taste them next time.
choices.feedback: Over-the-top polite — clashes hard with the easy ㅋㅋ tone of the chat.

choices.en: What's a financier? I'm not interested.
choices.feedback: Saying you're not interested shuts the whole conversation down after they opened up.

buddyCard.instructionKo: 최근 베이킹을 시작한 친한 친구 역할을 해 주세요. 스트레스를 풀려고 시작했다고 말하고, 얼마나 했는지와 최근 무엇을 만들었는지 이야기해 주세요. 학습자는 초급이니 천천히 말해 주세요.
buddyCard.reactionKo: 다음에는 내가 만든 것도 하나 줄게!

conversations.title: Suggesting a drink after work
conversations.situation: It's Friday and you text a friend to see if they want to grab a drink tonight.
conversations.tip: To make a casual plan, lead with a reaction to what they said, then pitch it with ~하자/~할래?. 한잔하자 and 콜 are how friends really lock in drinks.

turns.ko: 아 오늘 금요일이네 드디어ㅋㅋ
turns.romanization: a oneul geumyoirine deudieokk
turns.en: Ah it's finally Friday lol

turns.prompt: Agree that Friday has finally arrived and float the idea of a drink tonight.

choices.en: Right lol wanna grab a quick drink tonight?
choices.feedback: 그니까 agrees, then 한잔할래? pitches the plan — exactly how friends start this.

choices.en: Is drinking possible today? (formal)
choices.feedback: 금일/가능하십니까 is stiff business-speak. Friends say 오늘 한잔할래?

choices.en: Yeah, it's Friday.
choices.feedback: Just confirms the fact and stalls — it doesn't pitch a plan or keep things moving.

turns.ko: 오 콜 좋지ㅋㅋ 어디서 볼까?
turns.romanization: o kol jochikk eodiseo bolkka?
turns.en: Oh deal, sounds good lol where should we meet?

turns.prompt: Suggest meeting near the station and toss the time back to them.

choices.en: How about Gangnam Station? What time wanna meet?
choices.feedback: Concrete spot + 몇 시에 볼래? bounces it back so the plan keeps rolling.

choices.en: I'll announce the location later. (formal)
choices.feedback: 공지하겠습니다 sounds like an office memo — way too formal for a friend.

choices.en: Where should we meet?
choices.feedback: Just repeats their question instead of answering it — the plan goes nowhere.

turns.ko: 강남 좋아 그럼 7시쯤?
turns.romanization: gangnam joa geureom 7sijjeum?
turns.en: Gangnam works, so around 7?

turns.prompt: Confirm 7 and say you'll text when you arrive.

choices.en: Deal, 7! I'll text when I get there
choices.feedback: 콜 + 도착하면 톡할게 locks it in with a natural casual sign-off.

choices.en: I'm scheduled to arrive at 19:00. (formal)
choices.feedback: 19시/도착 예정입니다 reads like a train announcement, not a friend.

choices.en: Wanna grab a drink today?
choices.feedback: You already agreed — re-asking the original question makes no sense here.

buddyCard.instructionKo: 금요일 퇴근 뒤에 한잔하고 싶은 친한 친구 역할을 해 주세요. 오늘 만날 수 있는지 물어보고, 장소와 시간을 함께 정해 주세요. 학습자는 초급이니 천천히 말해 주세요.
buddyCard.reactionKo: 좋아, 그럼 일곱 시에 역에서 보자!

conversations.title: Inviting a friend for coffee
conversations.situation: You haven't seen a friend in a while and text them to grab coffee this weekend.
conversations.tip: 오랜만 (long time) and a soft 우리 ~할까? are perfect for casual invites. React first, then ask a follow-up to nail down the details.

turns.ko: 헐 우리 진짜 오랜만이다
turns.romanization: heol uri jinjja oraenmanida
turns.en: Whoa it's been so long since we last saw each other

turns.prompt: Agree it's been ages and suggest meeting for coffee soon.

choices.en: I know, ugh, should we grab coffee soon?
choices.feedback: Matches their energy, then 커피 한잔할까? is the natural soft invite.

choices.en: I'd like to treat you to tea after so long. (formal)
choices.feedback: 대접하고 싶습니다 is overly polite and old-fashioned for a close friend.

choices.en: Yeah, it's been a while.
choices.feedback: Agrees but stops there — no invite, so the chat just fizzles.

turns.ko: 완전 좋지! 언제 볼까?
turns.romanization: wanjeon jochi! eonje bolkka?
turns.en: Totally down! When should we meet?

turns.prompt: Propose Saturday afternoon and check if it works for them.

choices.ko: 토요일 오후 어때? 너 시간 돼?
choices.romanization: toyoil ohu eottae? neo sigan dwae?
choices.en: How about Saturday afternoon? You free?
choices.feedback: Gives a concrete time + 너 시간 돼? keeps it collaborative and moving.

choices.en: Please confirm your schedule. (formal)
choices.feedback: 귀하/부탁드립니다 is corporate email language, not a text to a friend.

choices.en: I like coffee.
choices.feedback: Doesn't answer when to meet — it drifts off the actual plan.

turns.ko: 토요일 좋아 근데 어디서 봐?
turns.romanization: toyoil joa geunde eodiseo bwa?
turns.en: Saturday's good, but where are we meeting?

turns.prompt: Suggest a cafe near them and offer to send the location.

choices.ko: 너네 동네 카페 갈까? 위치 보내줄게
choices.romanization: neone dongne kape galkka? wichi bonaejulge
choices.en: Wanna go to a cafe in your area? I'll send the spot
choices.feedback: Picks a place + 위치 보내줄게 is exactly how friends wrap up details.

choices.en: I'll inform you separately once a venue is chosen. (formal)
choices.feedback: 별도 안내드리겠습니다 sounds like an event invite, not a casual chat.

choices.en: How about Saturday afternoon?
choices.feedback: You already settled on Saturday — repeating it stalls the plan.

turns.ko: 오키 그럼 토요일에 봐!
turns.romanization: oki geureom toyoire bwa!
turns.en: Okay, see you Saturday then!

turns.prompt: Say you're looking forward to it.

choices.en: Nice, can't wait, see you then!
choices.feedback: 기대된다 + a quick 그때 봐 is a warm, natural way to close. (이따 봐 would mean 'later today,' but the plan is Saturday.)

choices.en: I'll see you then. (formal)
choices.feedback: 뵙겠습니다 is honorific — too formal to end a chat with a friend.

choices.en: Should we grab coffee?
choices.feedback: The plan's already set — re-inviting just loops back awkwardly.

buddyCard.instructionKo: 오랜만에 만나는 친한 친구 역할을 해 주세요. 이번 주말에 커피를 마실 수 있는지 물어보고, 토요일 오후의 장소를 함께 정해 주세요. 학습자는 초급이니 천천히 말해 주세요.

conversations.title: Asking a friend to work out together
conversations.situation: You want to start going to the gym and text a friend to join you so you'll actually stick with it.
conversations.tip: 같이 ~하자 and 운동 talk are super common between friends. Bouncing back 너는? and 언제부터? keeps a plan-making chat alive.

turns.ko: 요즘 운동 좀 해야 되는데 의지가 없다ㅋㅋ
turns.romanization: yojeum undong jom haeya doeneunde uijiga eopsdakk
turns.en: I really should work out these days but I have zero willpower lol

turns.prompt: Say same here and suggest hitting the gym together.

choices.en: Same lol wanna hit the gym together?
choices.feedback: 나도 bonds over it, then 같이 헬스 다닐래? turns it into a real plan.

choices.en: I recommend regular exercise. (formal)
choices.feedback: 권장드립니다 sounds like a health pamphlet — not how a friend talks.

choices.en: Exercise is good for your health.
choices.feedback: True but preachy — it doesn't invite them or move toward a plan.

turns.ko: 오 좋은데? 같이 하면 진짜 갈 듯ㅋㅋ
turns.romanization: o joeunde? gachi hamyeon jinjja gal deutkk
turns.en: Oh nice? I'd actually go if we did it together lol

turns.prompt: Agree it's easier together and ask when they want to start.

choices.ko: 그치 혼자는 안 가게 되잖아ㅋㅋ 언제부터 할까?
choices.romanization: geuchi honjaneun an gage doejanakk eonjebuteo halkka?
choices.en: Right, you never go alone lol when should we start?
choices.feedback: 그치 agrees, and 언제부터 할까? pushes the plan to the next step.

choices.en: The effects of partnered exercise are proven. (formal)
choices.feedback: 입증되었습니다 reads like a research paper — totally off for friends.

choices.en: Gyms are usually expensive.
choices.feedback: Changes the subject to cost and kills the momentum of the plan.

turns.ko: 다음 주 월요일부터 어때? 아침에ㅋㅋ
turns.romanization: daeum ju woryoilbuteo eottae? achimekk
turns.en: How about starting next Monday? In the morning lol

turns.prompt: React to 'morning' and ask what time exactly.

choices.ko: 헐 아침ㅋㅋ 좋아 몇 시에 만날까?
choices.romanization: heol achimkk joa myeot sie mannalkka?
choices.en: Whoa morning lol okay what time should we meet?
choices.feedback: A playful reaction + 몇 시에 만날까? keeps it casual and nails the detail.

choices.en: I agree to the morning workout schedule. (formal)
choices.feedback: 동의합니다 is contract language — friends just say 좋아.

choices.en: How about starting next Monday?
choices.feedback: That's literally what they just asked — echoing it stalls the chat.

turns.ko: 7시 어때? 운동하고 출근하게ㅋㅋ
turns.romanization: 7si eottae? undonghago chulgeunhagekk
turns.en: How about 7? So we can work out then head to work lol

turns.prompt: Confirm 7 and hype them up to not bail.

choices.en: Deal, 7! Let's really not skip lol
choices.feedback: 콜 locks the time and 빠지지 말자 adds friendly accountability — perfect close.

choices.ko: 결석 시 불이익이 있을 수 있습니다.
choices.romanization: gyeolseok si buriigi isseul su itseumnida.
choices.en: There may be penalties for absence. (formal)
choices.feedback: 결석/불이익 is school/work jargon — bizarre between friends.

choices.en: Wanna go to the gym?
choices.feedback: You already agreed and set a time — re-asking restarts the whole thing.

buddyCard.instructionKo: 같이 운동을 시작하고 싶은 친한 친구 역할을 해 주세요. 다음 주 월요일 아침이 괜찮은지와 몇 시에 만날지 물어보고, 빠지지 말자고 가볍게 약속해 주세요. 학습자는 초급이니 천천히 말해 주세요.
buddyCard.reactionKo: 좋아, 이번에는 우리 진짜 꾸준히 해 보자!

conversations.title: Friend bombed an exam
conversations.situation: A friend texts you, upset that they did terribly on a test.
conversations.tip: When a friend vents, lead with empathy (헐, 어떡해, 고생했어) before asking what happened — comforting first, then a follow-up question, is the natural flow.

turns.ko: 나 시험 완전 망했어ㅠㅠ
turns.romanization: na siheom wanjeon manghaesseoyuyu
turns.en: I totally bombed the exam ㅠㅠ

turns.prompt: React with sympathy and ask how bad it was.

choices.en: Oh no. Was it really hard?
choices.feedback: 헐 어떡해 reacts with concern, then 많이 어려웠어? gently asks what happened.

choices.en: Your exam results were poor (formal).
choices.feedback: Way too formal and stiff — friends never talk like this.

choices.en: I bombed my exam too.
choices.feedback: Makes it about you instead of comforting them first.

turns.ko: 응 한 문제도 제대로 못 풀었어 진짜ㅠ
turns.romanization: eung han munjedo jedaero mot pureosseo jinjjayu
turns.en: Yeah I couldn't even solve a single question properly ㅠ

turns.prompt: Show you feel for them and tell them not to stress too much.

choices.en: Aw… don't stress about it too much
choices.feedback: 아이고 + 스트레스받지 마 is warm, casual comfort.

choices.en: You should have studied harder (formal/scolding).
choices.feedback: Scolding and formal — the opposite of comforting a friend.

choices.en: So what'd you get?
choices.feedback: Prying for the number right now feels cold when they're already down.

turns.ko: 위로해 줘서 고마워ㅠㅠ 술이나 마시러 갈까
turns.romanization: wirohae jwoseo gomawoyuyu surina masireo galkka
turns.en: Thanks for comforting me ㅠㅠ Wanna go grab a drink or something?

turns.prompt: Agree and offer to treat them.

choices.en: Deal! I'll treat you today
choices.feedback: 콜 + 내가 쏠게 is super natural — agreeing and offering to pay.

choices.en: I do not drink (formal).
choices.feedback: Too formal, and it shuts the plan down.

choices.en: Do well on the next exam (polite).
choices.feedback: -세요 is polite, but it mismatches the close-friend register and ignores the invitation.

turns.ko: 오 진짜? 역시 너밖에 없다
turns.romanization: o jinjja? yeoksi neobakke eopsda
turns.en: Oh really? You're the best, seriously

turns.prompt: Brush it off and say let's go.

choices.en: Of course lol see you later!
choices.feedback: 당연하지 + 이따 보자 is the perfect casual wrap-up.

choices.en: Don't mention it (polite).
choices.feedback: 별말씀을요 is polite/formal — friends say 당연하지 or 뭘ㅋㅋ.

choices.en: Then I'll take my leave (very formal).
choices.feedback: Extremely formal sign-off — completely wrong for a friend.

buddyCard.instructionKo: 시험을 망쳐서 속상한 친한 친구 역할을 해 주세요. 학습자가 위로하면 같이 술을 마시러 갈지 물어봐 주세요. 학습자는 초급이니 천천히 말하고, 못 알아들으면 한 번 더 말해 주세요.

conversations.title: Buried in assignments
conversations.situation: A friend texts that they're drowning in assignments all due at once.
conversations.tip: Commiserating (나도, 그니까, 헐) signals you're on their side; pair it with a question like 언제까지야? to keep the venting going.

turns.ko: 과제가 산더미야 진짜 죽겠다
turns.romanization: gwajega sandeomiya jinjja jukgetda
turns.en: I've got a mountain of assignments, I'm seriously dying

turns.prompt: React and ask when they're due.

choices.en: Whoa, how many? When are they due?
choices.feedback: 헐 + two quick follow-ups keeps them venting and shows you care.

choices.en: You must be struggling with so much work (polite).
choices.feedback: 요 makes it formal — friends drop the 요.

choices.en: It's better to do assignments ahead of time.
choices.feedback: Sounds preachy — not what they want to hear mid-panic.

turns.ko: 세 개… 셋 다 내일까지야ㅋㅋㅋ 망했어
turns.romanization: se gae… set da naeilkkajiyakkk manghaesseo
turns.en: Three… all three are due tomorrow lol I'm doomed.

turns.prompt: Empathize hard.

choices.en: What, how are you gonna finish all that ㅠㅠ
choices.feedback: Genuine 'how is that even possible' empathy — exactly right.

choices.en: That is a very difficult situation (formal).
choices.feedback: Stiff, textbook phrasing — no friend texts like this.

choices.en: I already finished all mine.
choices.feedback: Bragging while they're stressed — reads as rubbing it in.

turns.ko: 그니까ㅠㅠ 밤새야 될 듯
turns.romanization: geunikkayuyu bamsaeya doel deut
turns.en: Right ㅠㅠ I'll probably have to pull an all-nighter

turns.prompt: Cheer them on and offer help.

choices.ko: 할 수 있어! 모르는 거 있음 물어봐
choices.romanization: hal su isseo! moreuneun geo isseum mureobwa
choices.en: You can do it! Ask me if you get stuck on anything
choices.feedback: Encouragement + an offer to help is warm and natural.

choices.en: Staying up all night is bad for your health (formal).
choices.feedback: Lecturing and formal — kills the supportive vibe.

choices.en: So how many assignments was it again?
choices.feedback: Just repeats a question they already answered.

turns.ko: 고마워ㅠㅠ 진짜 힘난다
turns.romanization: gomawoyuyu jinjja himnanda
turns.en: Thanks ㅠㅠ That really cheered me up.

turns.prompt: Tell them to hang in there.

choices.en: You got this!! Hit me up when you're done
choices.feedback: 화이팅 + 끝나면 연락해 is the classic casual send-off.

choices.en: Then I hope you work hard (formal).
choices.feedback: Overly formal — friends say 화이팅 or 파이팅.

choices.en: What's the assignment topic?
choices.feedback: Opens a new question when the chat is wrapping up.

buddyCard.instructionKo: 과제가 세 개나 밀려서 힘든 친한 친구 역할을 해 주세요. 무엇부터 해야 할지 모르겠다고 말하고, 도와줄 수 있는지 물어봐 주세요. 학습자는 초급이니 천천히 말해 주세요.

conversations.title: Let's study together
conversations.situation: A friend texts that the exam is close and they have not started studying, so you suggest studying together.
conversations.tip: Proposing plans casually (~할래?, ~하자, 콜) and locking in details (몇 시? 어디서?) is how friends turn an idea into an actual hangout.

turns.ko: 아 시험 코앞인데 하나도 안 했어
turns.romanization: a siheom koapinde hanado an haesseo
turns.en: Ugh the exam's right around the corner and I haven't done a thing

turns.prompt: Say you're the same and suggest studying together.

choices.en: Same lol wanna study together?
choices.feedback: 나도 (relate) + 같이 공부할래? (proposal) is a perfect casual invite.

choices.en: How would it be to study together? (very formal).
choices.feedback: Textbook-formal — no friend phrases an invite like this.

choices.en: It's better to study alone.
choices.feedback: Shoots down the chance to make a plan together.

turns.ko: 오 좋아! 어디서 할까?
turns.romanization: o joa! eodiseo halkka?
turns.en: Oh nice! Where should we do it?

turns.prompt: Suggest a cafe and ask if it works.

choices.ko: 학교 앞 카페 어때? 거기 조용하잖아
choices.romanization: hakgyo ap kape eottae? geogi joyonghajana
choices.en: How about the cafe by school? It's quiet there
choices.feedback: A concrete spot + 거기 조용하잖아 gives a reason and keeps it moving.

choices.en: You decide the place (formal).
choices.feedback: 당신 and 정하세요 are stiff — friends just throw out an idea.

choices.en: The library has no seats.
choices.feedback: Only says where NOT to go without suggesting anything.

turns.ko: 콜! 몇 시에 만날까?
turns.romanization: kol! myeot sie mannalkka?
turns.en: Deal! What time should we meet?

turns.prompt: Propose 2 PM and check it's okay.

choices.ko: 두 시 어때? 점심 먹고 가자
choices.romanization: du si eottae? jeomsim meokgo gaja
choices.en: How about 2? Let's go after lunch
choices.feedback: Names a time + 점심 먹고 가자 — natural and locks in the plan.

choices.en: I will see you at 2 PM (formal).
choices.feedback: 뵙겠습니다 is honorific — way too formal for a friend.

choices.en: I don't eat breakfast.
choices.feedback: Off-topic — they asked about the meeting time.

turns.ko: 오케이! 그럼 이따 봐
turns.romanization: okei! geureom itta bwa
turns.en: Okay! See you later then

turns.prompt: Confirm and tell them to bring their notes.

choices.en: K, make sure you bring your notes lol
choices.feedback: ㅇㅋ + a quick casual reminder is exactly how friends sign off.

choices.en: Please bring your notes (formal).
choices.feedback: 지참해 주시기 바랍니다 sounds like an official notice — far too formal.

choices.en: By the way, what's the exam range?
choices.feedback: Opens a brand-new question just as you're saying bye.

buddyCard.instructionKo: 시험공부를 같이 하자는 제안을 받은 친한 친구 역할을 해 주세요. 어디서 몇 시에 만날지 차례로 물어봐 주세요. 학습자는 초급이니 천천히 말해 주세요.

conversations.title: Making weekend plans
conversations.situation: A friend texts you to see if you want to hang out this weekend.
conversations.tip: With friends, keep replies short and toss back a question (왜?, 뭐 볼까?) to keep the conversation rolling.

turns.ko: 주말에 뭐 해?
turns.romanization: jumare mwo hae?
turns.en: What are you up to this weekend?

turns.prompt: Say nothing's planned and ask why.

choices.en: Nothing much, why?
choices.feedback: Natural — 왜? bounces it back and keeps the chat going.

choices.en: I have no plans.
choices.feedback: Too formal for a friend. Drop to 반말: 별거 없어.

choices.en: Have a good weekend.
choices.feedback: That ends the conversation instead of continuing it.

turns.ko: 같이 영화 볼래?
turns.romanization: gachi yeonghwa bollae?
turns.en: Wanna watch a movie together?

turns.prompt: Agree happily and ask what to watch.

choices.en: Sounds good! What should we watch?
choices.feedback: 좋아 + a follow-up question is exactly how friends keep momentum.

choices.en: Hmm, not really.
choices.feedback: That shuts the plan down — fine if true, but not 'keeping it going'.

choices.en: I like movies.
choices.feedback: Doesn't actually answer the invitation.

turns.ko: 그럼 토요일 저녁 어때?
turns.romanization: geureom toyoil jeonyeok eottae?
turns.en: Then how about Saturday evening?

turns.prompt: Confirm Saturday and say you'll text later.

choices.en: Saturday evening works. I'll text you later!
choices.feedback: This confirms the proposed evening, and 이따 톡할게 is a natural casual sign-off.

choices.en: I have time on Saturday.
choices.feedback: Stiff. With a friend: 토요일 좋아.

choices.en: Goodbye (formal).
choices.feedback: Way too formal to end a chat with a friend.

buddyCard.instructionKo: 이번 주말에 시간이 있는지 묻는 친한 친구 역할을 해 주세요. 같이 영화를 보자고 제안하고, 가능한 시간도 물어봐 주세요. 학습자는 초급이니 천천히 말해 주세요.

conversations.title: Deciding what to eat
conversations.situation: You and a friend are hanging out and getting hungry.
conversations.tip: 땡기다 (to crave), 콜 (deal!), and 가자 (let's go) are everyday casual staples between friends.

turns.ko: 배고프다… 뭐 먹지?
turns.romanization: baegopeuda… mwo meokji?
turns.en: I'm hungry… what should we eat?

turns.prompt: Say you don't mind and ask what they're craving.

choices.en: Anything's fine. What are you craving?
choices.feedback: 넌 뭐 땡겨? is very natural casual Korean for 'what do you feel like?'.

choices.en: Anything is fine with me.
choices.feedback: Correct grammar, but too formal among friends.

choices.en: Let's eat (formal).
choices.feedback: 읍시다 is stiff — friends say 먹자.

turns.ko: 음… 떡볶이 어때?
turns.romanization: eum… tteokbokki eottae?
turns.en: Hmm… how about tteokbokki?

turns.prompt: Love the idea and suggest a place.

choices.ko: 오 좋아! 학교 앞 거기 갈까?
choices.romanization: o joa! hakgyo ap geogi galkka?
choices.en: Oh nice! Should we go to that place by school?
choices.feedback: Enthusiasm + a concrete suggestion keeps the plan moving.

choices.en: Tteokbokki is spicy.
choices.feedback: A fact, but it doesn't move the plan forward.

choices.en: Right.
choices.feedback: This neither accepts nor rejects the suggestion, and -요 mismatches the close-friend register.

turns.ko: 콜! 지금 갈까?
turns.romanization: kol! jigeum galkka?
turns.en: Deal! Shall we go now?

turns.prompt: Agree and say let's go.

choices.en: Deal, let's go!
choices.feedback: 가자 is the casual 'let's go' — perfect.

choices.en: Yes, I will go (formal).
choices.feedback: Too formal — 가자 fits a friend.

choices.en: Could you please wait? (polite)
choices.feedback: Over-polite for a close friend.

buddyCard.instructionKo: 배가 고픈 친한 친구 역할을 해 주세요. 무엇을 먹을지 물은 뒤, 떡볶이는 어떤지 제안해 주세요. 학습자는 초급이니 천천히 말해 주세요.

conversations.title: Reacting to a friend's news
conversations.situation: A friend excitedly texts you that they saw a celebrity.
conversations.tip: Reactions (헐, 대박, 부럽다) plus a quick question (누구?, 사진 찍었어?) are the heart of casual Korean chatting.

turns.ko: 나 오늘 길에서 연예인 봤어!
turns.romanization: na oneul gireseo yeonyein bwasseo!
turns.en: I saw a celebrity on the street today!

turns.prompt: React with surprise and ask who it was.

choices.en: What, really? Who?
choices.feedback: 헐 진짜? (reaction) + 누구? (follow-up) is textbook casual chatting.

choices.en: I see (polite).
choices.feedback: Flat and formal — friends react bigger than this.

choices.en: Congratulations.
choices.feedback: Doesn't fit — there's nothing to congratulate.

turns.ko: 아이유! 카페에서 봤어ㅋㅋ
turns.romanization: aiyu! kapeeseo bwasseokk
turns.en: IU! I saw her at a cafe lol

turns.prompt: Show you're jealous and ask if they got a photo.

choices.en: No way, I'm jealous… did you take a photo?
choices.feedback: 대박 + 부럽다 + a follow-up keeps the energy up.

choices.en: Did you take a photo? (formal)
choices.feedback: Too formal — just say 사진 찍었어?

choices.en: I like IU too (polite).
choices.feedback: 요 is a touch formal, and it turns the spotlight onto you.

turns.ko: 당연하지ㅋㅋ 이따 보여줄게
turns.romanization: dangyeonhajikk itta boyeojulge
turns.en: Of course lol I'll show you later

turns.prompt: Say you can't wait.

choices.en: Oh I can't wait!
choices.feedback: 완전 + 기대된다 is natural casual excitement.

choices.en: I will look forward to it (formal).
choices.feedback: Stiff — friends say 기대된다.

choices.en: Understood (formal).
choices.feedback: Cold and formal for a fun chat.

buddyCard.instructionKo: 오늘 길에서 유명인을 본 친한 친구 역할을 해 주세요. 신나게 소식을 전하고, 누구를 봤을 것 같은지 물어봐 주세요. 학습자는 초급이니 천천히 말해 주세요.

conversations.title: Which top looks better
conversations.situation: A friend sends two fitting-room selfies and asks you to pick which top to buy.
conversations.tip: When a friend asks you to choose between two things, don't just say 'both nice' — react (오/음), pick a side, and give a quick reason. A clear opinion with a why is what they actually want.

turns.ko: 야 이거 둘 중에 뭐가 나아?? 사진 보냈어ㅋㅋ
turns.romanization: ya igeo dul junge mwoga naa?? sajin bonaesseokk
turns.en: Hey which of these two is better?? I sent pics lol

turns.prompt: React and ask what the occasion is before choosing.

choices.ko: 오 둘 다 예쁜데ㅋㅋ 어디 입고 갈 건데?
choices.romanization: o dul da yeppeundekk eodi ipgo gal geonde?
choices.en: Oh they're both cute lol where are you gonna wear it?
choices.feedback: 오 reacts, and 어디 입고 갈 건데? gets the context you need to actually help — keeps it rolling.

choices.en: Both suit you well. (formal)
choices.feedback: 어울리십니다 is way too formal for texting a friend about clothes — drop the 십니다.

choices.en: Buying clothes again? Your closet's gonna explode.
choices.feedback: Reads as nagging when they just want a quick opinion.

turns.ko: 주말에 소개팅ㅋㅋㅋ 첫인상 중요하잖아
turns.romanization: jumare sogaetingkkk cheosinsang jungyohajana
turns.en: A blind date this weekend lol first impressions matter you know

turns.prompt: Pick the white one and give a quick reason.

choices.ko: 헐 소개팅?? 그럼 무조건 흰색! 깔끔해 보여
choices.romanization: heol sogaeting?? geureom mujogeon huinsaek! kkalkkeumhae boyeo
choices.en: Whoa a blind date?? then definitely the white one! looks clean
choices.feedback: Reacts to the news and commits to a pick with a reason (깔끔해 보여) — exactly the help they asked for.

choices.en: The white top looks more tidy. (formal)
choices.feedback: 단정해 보입니다 is textbook-stiff — friends say 깔끔해 보여.

choices.en: I can't tell which one's better.
choices.feedback: Dodges the question — they asked you to choose, so just pick one.

turns.ko: 오 그치? 근데 흰색은 음식 흘리면 티 나잖아ㅠ
turns.romanization: o geuchi? geunde huinsaegeun eumsi keullimyeon ti najanayu
turns.en: Oh right? but white shows stains if I spill food ㅠ

turns.prompt: Agree but reassure her and tell her to just be careful.

choices.ko: ㅋㅋㅋ 그건 그래 근데 조심하면 되지! 흰색이 훨 나아
choices.romanization: kkk geugeon geurae geunde josimhamyeon doeji! huinsaegi hwol naa
choices.en: Lol true but just be careful! white's way better
choices.feedback: 그건 그래 validates her worry, then you hold your pick — natural back-and-forth that lands the decision.

choices.ko: 흰 옷은 오염에 취약하므로 주의가 필요합니다.
choices.romanization: huin oseun oyeome chwiyakameuro juuiga piryohamnida.
choices.en: White clothes are prone to stains so caution is needed. (formal)
choices.feedback: Sounds like a care-label warning, not a friend hyping her up.

choices.en: Then just buy the black one.
choices.feedback: Flip-flops the second she hesitates — wishy-washy when she wanted you to be sure.

turns.ko: ㅇㅋㅋㅋ 결정했어 흰색 살게! 고마워
turns.romanization: ngkkk gyeoljeonghaesseo huinsaek salge! gomawo
turns.en: Okok lol decided, I'll get the white one! thanks

turns.prompt: Hype her up and tell her to send a full pic after.

choices.ko: ㅋㅋ 잘 골랐어! 입고 풀샷 한 번 보내봐
choices.romanization: kk jal gollasseo! ipgo pulsya tan beon bonaebwa
choices.en: Lol good pick! put it on and send me a full shot
choices.feedback: 잘 골랐어 closes it warmly and 풀샷 보내봐 keeps the thread alive — perfect casual sign-off.

choices.en: An excellent choice. Please send a photo. (formal)
choices.feedback: Reads like a shop clerk — friends say 잘 골랐어 / 보내봐.

choices.ko: 소개팅 잘 안 되면 옷 탓이야ㅋㅋ
choices.romanization: sogaeting jal an doemyeon ot tasiyakk
choices.en: If the date flops it's the outfit's fault lol
choices.feedback: Joke lands flat — adds pressure right when she finally felt good about it.

buddyCard.instructionKo: 쇼핑 중인 친한 친구 역할을 해 주세요. 상의 두 벌 중 무엇이 더 나은지 묻고, 고른 이유도 물어봐 주세요. 학습자는 초급이니 천천히 말해 주세요.

conversations.title: Should I get a new phone
conversations.situation: A friend texts that their phone keeps dying and they're torn about whether to upgrade.
conversations.tip: When a friend is on the fence about a purchase, ask a probing question (왜? / 얼마나 됐는데?) before giving advice. Drawing out the details is how friends help each other decide.

turns.ko: 아 진짜 폰 바꿀까 말까 고민된다…
turns.romanization: a jinjja pon bakkulkka malkka gomindoenda…
turns.en: Ugh should I get a new phone or not… I keep going back and forth

turns.prompt: Ask what's wrong with the current one.

choices.ko: 갑자기? 지금 폰 왜, 뭐 문제 있어?
choices.romanization: gapjagi? jigeum pon wae, mwo munje isseo?
choices.en: Out of nowhere? what's up with your phone, something wrong?
choices.feedback: 왜 + 뭐 문제 있어? digs into the reason before advising — that's how you actually help them decide.

choices.en: Are you considering replacing your device? (formal)
choices.feedback: 교체를 고려 중이신가요 sounds like a carrier rep — say 폰 왜, 문제 있어?

choices.en: Yeah change it change it.
choices.feedback: Snap advice with zero context — you don't even know what's wrong yet.

turns.ko: 배터리가 반나절도 안 가ㅠㅠ 산 지 4년 됐거든
turns.romanization: baeteoriga bannajeoldo an gayuyu san ji 4nyeon dwaetgeodeun
turns.en: The battery doesn't even last half a day ㅠㅠ I've had it 4 years

turns.prompt: React that 4 years is a lot and lean toward upgrading.

choices.ko: 헐 4년이면 오래 썼네ㅋㅋ 그 정도면 바꿀 때 됐지
choices.romanization: heol 4nyeonimyeon orae sseonnekk geu jeongdomyeon bakkul ttae dwaetji
choices.en: Whoa 4 years is a long time lol at that point it's time to upgrade
choices.feedback: 헐 reacts to the detail and 바꿀 때 됐지 gives a clear, reasoned nudge — exactly what they're fishing for.

choices.en: If you've used it 4 years I recommend replacement. (formal)
choices.feedback: 권장드립니다 is customer-service formal — friends say 바꿀 때 됐지.

choices.en: Four years? It's practically still a new phone.
choices.feedback: Four years is already a long replacement cycle, so this dismisses the battery problem instead of responding realistically.

turns.ko: 근데 새 폰 너무 비싸… 백만원 훌쩍 넘던데
turns.romanization: geunde sae pon neomu bissa… baengmanwon huljjeong neomdeonde
turns.en: but new phones are so expensive… way over a million won

turns.prompt: Sympathize and suggest a cheaper route like a deal or last year's model.

choices.ko: 그니까ㅋㅋ 미쳤어 요즘. 그냥 작년 모델 노려봐, 훨 싸
choices.romanization: geunikkakk michyeosseo yojeum. geunyang jangnyeon model noryeobwa, hwol ssa
choices.en: Right lol prices are insane these days. just go for last year's model, way cheaper
choices.feedback: 그니까 commiserates and you offer a real fix (작년 모델) — keeps solving the problem together.

choices.ko: 최신 기종은 가격대가 상당히 높은 편입니다.
choices.romanization: choesin gijongeun gagyeokdaega sangdanghi nopeun pyeonimnida.
choices.en: The latest models are in a fairly high price range. (formal)
choices.feedback: Just restates their point in stiff 습니다 form without offering anything.

choices.ko: 돈 없으면 그냥 쓰던 거 써.
choices.romanization: don eopseumyeon geunyang sseudeon geo sseo.
choices.en: If you're broke just keep using your old one.
choices.feedback: Comes off blunt and unhelpful — they wanted ideas, not a dead end.

turns.ko: 오 작년 모델! 그 생각은 못 했네ㅋㅋ 가성비 괜찮아?
turns.romanization: o jangnyeon model! geu saenggageun mo taennekk gaseongbi gwaenchana?
turns.en: Oh last year's model! didn't think of that lol is the value good?

turns.prompt: Confirm it's worth it and tell her to check it out.

choices.ko: ㅇㅇ 성능 거의 똑같은데 싸ㅋㅋ 한 번 알아봐!
choices.romanization: ngng seongneung geoui ttokgateunde ssakk han beon arabwa!
choices.en: Yep performance is basically the same but cheaper lol go check it out!
choices.feedback: Gives the verdict (가성비 좋다) and a nudge to act (알아봐!) — wraps the advice cleanly.

choices.en: In terms of value it's a very reasonable choice. (formal)
choices.feedback: Reads like a product review. Just say 싸고 좋아, 알아봐!

choices.en: Let me explain what 'value for money' means…
choices.feedback: She knows the word — explaining it derails the chat and sounds condescending.

buddyCard.instructionKo: 휴대폰을 바꿀지 고민하는 친한 친구 역할을 해 주세요. 배터리가 너무 빨리 닳는다고 말하고, 작년 제품도 괜찮은지 물어봐 주세요. 학습자는 초급이니 천천히 말해 주세요.

conversations.title: Help picking a friend's gift
conversations.situation: A friend texts you for help choosing a birthday gift for your mutual friend.
conversations.tip: When asked for a recommendation, ask about budget and the person's taste first (예산? 걔 뭐 좋아해?). Narrowing it down before suggesting is what makes the help genuinely useful.

turns.ko: 야 다음 주 지민이 생일인데 뭐 선물하지?? 도와줘ㅠ
turns.romanization: ya daeum ju jimini saengirinde mwo seonmulhaji?? dowajwoyu
turns.en: Hey it's Jimin's birthday next week, what should I get?? help me ㅠ

turns.prompt: Ask how much she's thinking of spending.

choices.ko: 오 벌써 생일이구나ㅋㅋ 예산 얼마 정도 생각해?
choices.romanization: o beolsseo saengirigunakk yesan eolma jeongdo saenggakae?
choices.en: Oh it's her birthday already lol how much are you thinking of spending?
choices.feedback: 예산 얼마? narrows it down right away — you can't recommend well without knowing the budget.

choices.en: What budget have you allocated? (formal)
choices.feedback: 책정하셨습니까 sounds like a finance meeting — say 예산 얼마 정도 생각해?

choices.en: It's the thought that counts with gifts.
choices.feedback: True but useless here — she asked for actual ideas, so help her brainstorm.

turns.ko: 한 5만 원 안쪽? 너무 부담 주긴 싫어서ㅋㅋ
turns.romanization: han 5man won anjjok? neomu budam jugin sireoseokk
turns.en: Like under 50k? Don't wanna make it too much lol.

turns.prompt: React, then ask about the friend's taste before suggesting.

choices.ko: 오케이 적당하네ㅋㅋ 근데 걔 요즘 뭐에 빠져 있어?
choices.romanization: okei jeokdanghanekk geunde gyae yojeum mwoe ppajyeo isseo?
choices.en: Okay, that's reasonable lol. But what's she into these days?
choices.feedback: Confirms the budget, then 뭐에 빠져 있어? asks about her taste before choosing a gift.

choices.en: That amount seems appropriate. (formal)
choices.feedback: 사료됩니다 is super stiff and old-fashioned — friends say 적당하네.

choices.en: Can you even buy anything for 50k?
choices.feedback: Sounds dismissive of her budget — plenty of good gifts fit, so stay constructive.

turns.ko: 요즘 향수에 진심이더라고ㅋㅋ 인스타에 맨날 올려
turns.romanization: yojeum hyangsue jinsimideoragokk inseutae maennal ollyeo
turns.en: She's really into perfume lately lol. She posts it on Instagram all the time.

turns.prompt: Light up and suggest a perfume or a diffuser.

choices.ko: 오 그럼 답 나왔네ㅋㅋ 디퓨저나 미니 향수 어때?
choices.romanization: o geureom dam nawannekk dipyujeona mini hyangsu eottae?
choices.en: Oh then we've got our answer lol how about a diffuser or a mini perfume?
choices.feedback: 답 나왔네 reacts, and two concrete options move the decision forward — solid recommending.

choices.ko: 향수 또는 디퓨저를 선물하시는 것을 추천드립니다.
choices.romanization: hyangsu ttoneun dipyujeoreul seonmulhasineun geoseul chucheondeurimnida.
choices.en: I recommend gifting a perfume or diffuser. (formal)
choices.feedback: 추천드립니다 reads like a shopping site. Just say 디퓨저나 향수 어때?

choices.en: Perfume's hard to pick since it's a taste thing.
choices.feedback: Shoots down the idea instead of running with the great lead she just gave you.

turns.ko: 오 디퓨저 좋다! 근데 어디서 사지? 추천 좀ㅋㅋ
turns.romanization: o dipyujeo jota! geunde eodiseo saji? chucheon jomkk
turns.en: Oh a diffuser's nice! but where do I buy it? give me a rec lol

turns.prompt: Offer to send a link to a shop you know.

choices.ko: 내가 자주 가는 데 있어ㅋㅋ 링크 보내줄게!
choices.romanization: naega jaju ganeun de isseokk ringkeu bonaejulge!
choices.en: There's a place I go to a lot lol I'll send you the link!
choices.feedback: Offers a concrete next step (링크 보내줄게) — exactly how friends hand off a rec and keep things moving.

choices.ko: 제가 즐겨 이용하는 매장 링크를 전송해 드리겠습니다.
choices.romanization: jega jeulgyeo iyonghaneun maejang ningkeureul jeonsonghae deurigetseumnida.
choices.en: I'll send you a link to the store I frequent. (formal)
choices.feedback: 전송해 드리겠습니다 is robotic — friends say 링크 보내줄게.

turns.ko: 굿굿ㅋㅋ 근데 우리 1박 2일이야 2박 3일이야?
turns.romanization: gutgutkk geunde uri 1bak 2iriya 2bak 3iriya?
turns.en: Good good lol, but are we doing one night and two days or two nights and three days?

turns.prompt: Suggest longer and check with them

choices.ko: 이왕 가는 거 2박 3일 어때? 1박 2일은 너무 짧잖아
choices.romanization: iwang ganeun geo 2bak 3il eottae? 1bak 2ireun neomu jjalbjana
choices.en: Since we're going anyway, how about two nights and three days? One night and two days is too short.
choices.feedback: Offers a specific longer plan, then gives a clear reason and checks with 어때.

choices.en: The trip duration will be announced at a later date.
choices.feedback: Reads like an official notice — totally out of place between friends.

choices.en: How many days is one night?
choices.feedback: Confuses a basic term — derails the chat and sounds clueless.

turns.ko: 오케이 2박 3일 좋아! 첫날부터 빡세게 놀자ㅋㅋ
turns.romanization: okei 2bak 3il joa! cheonnalbuteo ppaksege noljakk
turns.en: Okay two nights, love it! Let's party hard from day oneㅋㅋ

turns.prompt: Match the energy and wrap up

choices.ko: ㅋㅋㅋ 좋아, 맛집 리스트 짜서 공유할게! 완전 기대된다
choices.romanization: kkk joa, matjim niseuteu jjaseo gongyuhalge! wanjeon gidaedoenda
choices.en: Lol, nice. I'll make a restaurant list and share it! I'm so excited.
choices.feedback: This keeps the earlier task split, confirms the next step, and ends with matching excitement.

choices.ko: 일정표 작성 완료 시 송부해 드리겠습니다.
choices.romanization: iljeongpyo jakseong wallyo si songbuhae deurigetseumnida.
choices.en: I will dispatch the itinerary upon completion.
choices.feedback: Sounds like a memo to a client — wrong register for texting a friend.

choices.en: What does partying hard even mean?
choices.feedback: Questions an obvious phrase — flattens the hyped mood instead of matching it.

buddyCard.instructionKo: 함께 여행을 준비하는 친한 친구 역할을 해 주세요. 숙소 종류와 여행 기간을 물어보고, 서로 무엇을 알아볼지 정해 주세요. 학습자는 초급이니 한 번에 하나씩 물어봐 주세요.

conversations.title: Venting about working late
conversations.situation: A friend texts you at night complaining they're stuck at the office doing overtime again.
conversations.tip: When a friend vents, lead with a reaction (헐/진짜?) and a quick 되묻기 (왜?/언제 끝나?) so they feel heard — that's what keeps a venting chat alive.

turns.ko: 하… 나 아직 회사야 ㅠㅠ
turns.romanization: ha… na aji koesaya yuyu
turns.en: Ugh… I'm still at the office ㅠㅠ

turns.prompt: React with surprise and ask why they're still there.

choices.en: What, still?? Why are you working late again?
choices.feedback: 헐 (reaction) + 왜 또 야근해? (follow-up) is exactly how friends pick up a vent.

choices.en: Oh, you're still at the office. (formal)
choices.feedback: 계시는군요 is 존댓말 — way too formal for a friend venting.

choices.en: I'm kinda tired today too.
choices.feedback: Changes the subject to you instead of reacting to their complaint.

turns.ko: 내일까지 보고서 내야 돼서 ㅠㅠ 팀장이 갑자기 시킴
turns.romanization: naeilkkaji bogoseo naeya dwaeseo yuyu timjangi gapjagi sikim
turns.en: I have to hand in a report by tomorrow ㅠㅠ my team lead just dumped it on me

turns.prompt: Sympathize and ask when they'll be done.

choices.en: Wow that's so unfair… when do you finish?
choices.feedback: Empathy (너무하다) plus 언제 끝나? keeps the conversation going and shows you care.

choices.en: Shall I help you write the report? (formal)
choices.feedback: 드릴까요 is 존댓말 — friends would say 도와줄까?, and it's a sudden offer that skips the empathy.

choices.en: Still, you get paid lol
choices.feedback: Dismissive — invalidates the venting instead of being on their side.

turns.ko: 몰라 적어도 10시 ㅋㅋㅋ 진짜 퇴사하고 싶다
turns.romanization: molla jeogeodo 10si kkk jinjja toesahago sipda
turns.en: Dunno, at least 10pm lol I seriously wanna quit

turns.prompt: Sympathize and suggest a treat after work.

choices.en: You're really working so hard… how about chicken and beer after?
choices.feedback: 고생한다 + a fun plan (치맥) is the perfect friend move — comfort plus something to look forward to.

choices.en: You should decide on quitting carefully. (formal)
choices.feedback: Stiff lecture in 존댓말 — kills the mood when they just wanted to vent.

choices.en: 10pm? I'm already home though.
choices.feedback: Comes off as bragging and rubs in their bad situation.

turns.ko: 오 치맥 콜 ㅋㅋ 끝나면 톡할게
turns.romanization: o chimaek kol kk kkeunnamyeon tokalge
turns.en: Oh chicken and beer, deal lol I'll text you when I'm done

turns.prompt: Tell them to hang in there and you'll wait.

choices.en: Okay, hang in there! I'll be waiting
choices.feedback: 힘내 + 기다릴게 is a warm, natural casual send-off after a vent.

choices.en: Well then, keep up the good work. (formal)
choices.feedback: Very formal and distant; a close friend would naturally say 힘내 or 고생 많다.

choices.en: When's the report deadline again?
choices.feedback: Just repeats a question already answered — doesn't move the chat to a close.

buddyCard.instructionKo: 야근 때문에 지친 친한 친구 역할을 해 주세요. 아직 회사에 있다고 말하고, 갑자기 맡은 보고서 때문에 늦는다고 설명해 주세요. 학습자는 초급이니 짧게 말하고 위로나 제안을 기다려 주세요.

conversations.title: Thinking about quitting a part-time job
conversations.situation: A friend texts that they're seriously considering quitting their part-time job because the manager is awful.
conversations.tip: When a friend is weighing a decision, react then dig with 되묻기 (왜?/무슨 일 있었어?) before giving any opinion — friends gather the story first.

turns.ko: 나 알바 그만둘까 진지하게 고민 중이야
turns.romanization: na alba geumandulkka jinjihage gomin jungiya
turns.en: I'm seriously thinking about quitting my part-time job.

turns.prompt: React and ask what happened.

choices.en: What, out of nowhere? Did something happen?
choices.feedback: Reaction + 무슨 일 있었어? pulls the story out — the natural first response to a friend's big decision.

choices.en: You're planning to quit your part-time job? (formal)
choices.feedback: 그만두시려고요 is 존댓말, and 아르바이트 sounds textbook — friends say 알바 and 반말.

choices.en: Yeah good call, quit.
choices.feedback: Jumps to a verdict before hearing why — friends ask first.

turns.ko: 사장님이 자꾸 시간 막 바꾸고 어제는 괜히 나한테 짜증냄
turns.romanization: sajangnimi jakku sigan mak bakkugo eojeneun gwaenhi nahante jjajeungnaem
turns.en: The boss keeps changing my hours randomly and yesterday he snapped at me for no reason

turns.prompt: Take their side and ask how long they've put up with it.

choices.ko: 헐 진짜 별로다… 그런 거 참은 지 얼마나 됐어?
choices.romanization: heol jinjja byeolloda… geureon geo chameun ji eolmana dwaesseo?
choices.en: Ugh that's so lame… how long have you been putting up with that?
choices.feedback: Siding with them (별로다) + a follow-up keeps them talking and shows you're listening.

choices.en: The boss probably has his reasons too. (formal)
choices.feedback: Taking the boss's side in 존댓말 — the opposite of what a venting friend needs.

choices.en: How much do you get paid per hour?
choices.feedback: Random subject change to money — ignores the emotional point.

turns.ko: 한 세 달? 근데 막상 그만둔다 하니까 좀 무섭기도 하고
turns.romanization: han se dal? geunde maksang geumandunda hanikka jom museopgido hago
turns.en: Like three months? But now that I'm actually about to quit, it's kinda scary too

turns.prompt: Reassure them and gently nudge them to do what's best for them.

choices.ko: 그치 그 마음 이해돼. 그래도 너 힘들면 그만두는 게 맞지
choices.romanization: geuchi geu maeum ihaedwae. geuraedo neo himdeulmyeon geumanduneun ge matji
choices.en: Yeah, I get that feeling. Still, if it's wearing you out, quitting is the right call
choices.feedback: 그치 (맞장구) + understanding + a gentle opinion — supportive without bulldozing.

choices.en: I hope you won't regret it. (formal)
choices.feedback: Cold 존댓말 send-off — sounds like a stranger, not a friend.

choices.en: Scared of what? Just keep working there.
choices.feedback: Brushes off their fear and contradicts them — not how a supportive friend reacts.

turns.ko: 고마워 ㅠㅠ 너랑 얘기하니까 마음 정리된다
turns.romanization: gomawo yuyu neorang yaegihanikka maeum jeongnidoenda
turns.en: Thanks ㅠㅠ talking to you helps me sort my head out

turns.prompt: Offer to keep listening anytime.

choices.en: Tell me anytime lol let me know once you decide!
choices.feedback: Warm, open-ended, and asks to stay in the loop — a perfect friend close.

choices.en: I'm glad I could be of help. (formal)
choices.feedback: 다행입니다 is 존댓말 — too businesslike between close friends.

choices.ko: 그래서 결국 그만두는 거야 마는 거야?
choices.romanization: geuraeseo gyeolguk geumanduneun geoya maneun geoya?
choices.en: So are you quitting in the end or not?
choices.feedback: Pushy — pressures them for an answer right after they said they need to think.

buddyCard.instructionKo: 아르바이트를 그만둘지 고민하는 친한 친구 역할을 해 주세요. 사장님이 근무 시간을 자주 바꾸고 짜증을 냈다고 말한 뒤, 어떻게 하면 좋을지 물어봐 주세요. 학습자는 초급이니 천천히 말해 주세요.

conversations.title: Dreading a company dinner
conversations.situation: You two are hanging out when your friend groans about a forced company dinner (회식) they have to attend tonight.
conversations.tip: Face-to-face venting still runs on 맞장구 (헐/그니까) and 되묻기 (몇 차까지 가?) — match their energy out loud and keep the back-and-forth going.

turns.ko: 아 나 오늘 또 회식이야 가기 싫어 죽겠어
turns.romanization: a na oneul tto hoesigiya gagi sireo jukgesseo
turns.en: Ugh, I've got another company dinner tonight, I so don't wanna go

turns.prompt: React and ask why the company dinners happen so often.

choices.ko: 또? 왜 이렇게 자주 해 ㅋㅋ
choices.romanization: tto? wae ireoke jaju hae kk
choices.en: Again? Why do you guys do it so often lol
choices.feedback: 또? (맞장구) + 왜 자주 해? bounces it back and matches their groan.

choices.en: Are you reluctant to attend the dinner? (formal)
choices.feedback: 참석하기 싫으신가요 is 존댓말 — bizarrely formal when sitting right next to a friend.

choices.en: Company dinners are part of work life.
choices.feedback: Sounds like a lecture — doesn't sympathize or keep the chat casual.

turns.ko: 팀장이 술을 너무 좋아해서 ㅋㅋ 맨날 2차 3차 가
turns.romanization: timjangi sureul neomu joahaeseo kk maennal 2cha 3cha ga
turns.en: My team lead loves drinking lol we always go to a second and third round

turns.prompt: React to that and ask how late it usually runs.

choices.en: Whoa, up to a third round?? So what time does it end?
choices.feedback: Big reaction + 몇 시에 끝나? is genuine curiosity that keeps them venting.

choices.en: Drinking isn't good for your health. (formal)
choices.feedback: Preachy and in 존댓말 — totally kills a casual hangout vibe.

choices.en: I went to bed early yesterday though.
choices.feedback: Random and self-focused — ignores what they just said.

turns.ko: 기본 새벽 1시 ㅋㅋㅋ 진짜 집 가고 싶어
turns.romanization: gibon saebyeok 1si kkk jinjja jip gago sipeo
turns.en: Like 1am minimum lol I just wanna go home

turns.prompt: Sympathize hard and suggest a polite escape plan.

choices.ko: 와 그건 너무하다… 1차만 살짝 있다가 빠져!
choices.romanization: wa geugeon neomuhada… 1chaman saljjak itdaga ppajyeo!
choices.en: Wow that's too much… just stay for the first round and sneak out!
choices.feedback: 그건 너무하다 (empathy) + a practical tip is exactly the help a venting friend wants.

choices.en: Staying till the end is good manners. (formal)
choices.feedback: Formal etiquette lecture — the last thing they want to hear right now.

choices.en: 1am means the last train's already gone, take a taxi.
choices.feedback: Fixates on a logistics detail and skips the emotional support.

turns.ko: 그래야겠다 ㅋㅋ 적당히 마시고 튈게
turns.romanization: geuraeyagetda kk jeokdanghi masigo twilge
turns.en: I should do that lol I'll drink a bit and bail

turns.prompt: Cheer them on and tell them to text you after.

choices.ko: ㅋㅋㅋ 그래 적당히 해! 끝나고 톡해
choices.romanization: kkk geurae jeokdanghi hae! kkeunnago tokae
choices.en: Lol yeah, take it easy! Text me when it's over
choices.feedback: Light encouragement + 끝나고 톡해 wraps the hangout chat naturally.

choices.en: I hope you have a pleasant time. (formal)
choices.feedback: 존댓말 well-wishing sounds like a card, not a friend.

choices.en: Wait, why don't you wanna go to the dinner again?
choices.feedback: Re-asks something already explained — stalls instead of closing the chat.

buddyCard.instructionKo: 회식에 가기 싫은 친한 친구 역할을 해 주세요. 팀장님 때문에 늦게까지 술자리가 이어진다고 말하고, 일찍 나올 방법이 있을지 물어봐 주세요. 학습자는 초급이니 짧고 분명하게 말해 주세요.

conversations.title: Asking a close friend for a favor
conversations.situation: Your phone is about to die and you forgot your charger. You text a close friend to borrow theirs, ask for yesterday's class notes, and sheepishly borrow a little cash for the bus.
conversations.tip: With close friends, open with 부탁이 있는데 to flag the request, then soften with 미안한데 + a ~줄 수 있어? question. 반말 plus a casual 좀 makes it feel light, not demanding.

turns.ko: 어 왜? 무슨 일 있어?
turns.romanization: eo wae? museun il isseo?
turns.en: Oh hey, what's up? Something going on?

turns.prompt: Flag that you have a favor to ask before getting into it.

choices.ko: 어 부탁이 있는데… 들어줄 수 있어?
choices.romanization: eo butagi inneunde… deureojul su isseo?
choices.en: Hey, I've got a favor to ask… could you do it for me?
choices.feedback: 부탁이 있는데 prepares your friend before the request, and -줄 수 있어? asks without sounding demanding.

choices.en: Do what I'm asking. (sounds like an order)
choices.feedback: The command 들어 leaves your friend no room to respond and sounds demanding.

choices.en: Might I trouble you for a favor? (too formal for a close friend)
choices.feedback: 드려도 될까요 is polite and useful elsewhere, but it is too formal for this close-friend text.

turns.ko: 응 말해 봐, 뭔데?
turns.romanization: eung malhae bwa, mwonde?
turns.en: Sure, go ahead, what is it?

turns.prompt: Explain your phone is dying and ask to borrow their charger, softening it.

choices.ko: 미안한데 폰 배터리가 거의 다 돼서… 충전기 좀 빌려줄 수 있어?
choices.romanization: mianhande pon baeteoriga geoui da dwaeseo… chungjeongi jom billyeojul su isseo?
choices.en: Sorry to ask, my phone's almost out of battery… could you lend me your charger?
choices.feedback: 미안한데 softens the request, and 배터리가 거의 다 됐어 is the natural way to say the battery is nearly empty.

choices.en: Hand over your charger, my phone's dying. (rude/demanding)
choices.feedback: 내놔 is a forceful command, and 폰 죽어 sounds translated rather than natural Korean.

choices.en: Do you have a charger? (abrupt, leaves out the actual request)
choices.feedback: This only checks whether a charger exists; it never asks to borrow it.

turns.ko: 아 그럼! 내 가방에 보조배터리도 있어. 이따 만날 때 줄게. 또 필요한 거 없어?
turns.romanization: a geureom! nae gabange bojobaeteorido isseo. itta mannal ttae julge. tto piryohan geo eopseo?
turns.en: Oh, of course! I've got a power bank in my bag too. I'll give it to you when we meet. Anything else you need?

turns.prompt: Ask them to also bring yesterday's class notes for you.

choices.ko: 오 진짜? 고마워!! 아 그리고 어제 수업 필기한 것도 좀 가져다줄 수 있어?
choices.romanization: o jinjja? gomawo!! a geurigo eoje sueop pilgihan geotdo jom gajyeodajul su isseo?
choices.en: Oh really? Thank you!! Could you also bring the notes you took in class yesterday?
choices.feedback: The thanks comes first, and -것도 좀 가져다줄 수 있어? adds a second request gently.

choices.en: Obviously you have to bring the notes too. (entitled tone)
choices.feedback: 당연히 and -아야지 treat your friend's help as an obligation.

choices.en: Don't you dare not bring the notes. (pushy)
choices.feedback: This is a prohibition, not a request, so it sounds pushy even between close friends.

turns.ko: ㅋㅋ 알겠어 필기도 챙겨 갈게. 진짜 다른 건 없고?
turns.romanization: kk algesseo pilgido chaenggyeo galge. jinjja dareun geon eopsgo?
turns.en: Lol okay, I'll grab the notes too. You sure there's nothing else?

turns.prompt: Sheepishly ask to borrow a little cash for the bus since you left your card at home, and promise to pay it back.

choices.ko: 헐 진짜 미안한데… 나 카드를 집에 두고 와서 그런데 버스비로 이천 원만 빌려줄 수 있어? 이따 바로 갚을게
choices.romanization: heol jinjja mianhande… na kadeureul jibe dugo waseo geureonde beoseubiro icheon wonman billyeojul su isseo? itta baro gapeulge
choices.en: I'm really sorry… I left my card at home. Could you lend me just 2,000 won for the bus? I'll pay you back right away.
choices.feedback: The reason, small amount, -줄 수 있어?, and 갚을게 make the request specific and considerate.

choices.en: Lend me some money, 10,000 won. (blunt, no softening)
choices.feedback: This jumps straight to a larger amount without explaining why or promising to repay it.

choices.en: You've got 10,000 won, right? Just give it to me. (demanding)
choices.feedback: 그냥 줘 asks your friend to give you money rather than lend it and sounds entitled.

turns.ko: 괜찮아 ㅋㅋ 이따 보내. 만날 때 다 챙겨 갈게!
turns.romanization: gwaenchana kk itta bonae. mannal ttae da chaenggyeo galge!
turns.en: It's fine lol, send it later. I'll bring everything when we meet!

buddyCard.instructionKo: 부탁을 받는 친한 친구 역할을 해 주세요. 무슨 부탁인지 물어보고, 충전기나 수업 필기를 챙겨 주겠다고 말해 주세요. 학습자는 초급이니 한 번에 하나씩 물어봐 주세요.

conversations.title: Politely asking a coworker a favor
conversations.situation: You have to leave the office early for an appointment, so you politely ask a coworker if they could pass a document to the team lead and cover a client call while you're out.
conversations.tip: In 존댓말, lead with 혹시 부탁 좀 드려도 될까요? to ask permission first, then 죄송하지만 + ~해 주실 수 있을까요? for the actual request. 혹시 and 좀 are the magic softeners.

turns.ko: 네, 무슨 일 있으세요?
turns.romanization: ne, museun il isseuseyo?
turns.en: Yes, is something the matter?

turns.prompt: Politely ask permission to make a request before explaining.

choices.en: Could I possibly ask you a favor?
choices.feedback: 혹시 and -드려도 될까요? politely ask permission before you explain the favor.

choices.en: Do me a favor. (too blunt for a coworker)
choices.feedback: The request is grammatically polite, but the direct command 들어줘요 is too blunt for this coworker.

choices.en: I've got a favor, can you do it? (반말 — too casual at work)
choices.feedback: -줄 수 있어? is casual speech and mismatches the polite workplace conversation.

turns.ko: 그럼요, 말씀하세요.
turns.romanization: geureomyo, malsseumhaseyo.
turns.en: Of course, go ahead.

turns.prompt: Explain you have to leave early and ask if they could pass a document to the team lead.

choices.ko: 제가 오늘 좀 일찍 나가야 해서요. 죄송하지만 이 서류를 팀장님께 좀 전달해 주실 수 있을까요?
choices.romanization: jega oneul jom iljjing nagaya haeseoyo. joesonghajiman i seoryureul timjangnimkke jom jeondalhae jusil su isseulkkayo?
choices.en: I have to leave a bit early today. I'm sorry to ask, but could you pass this document to the team lead for me?
choices.feedback: The reason comes first, and 죄송하지만 plus -주실 수 있을까요? makes the workplace request considerate.

choices.ko: 저 먼저 갈게요. 이거 팀장님 주세요.
choices.romanization: jeo meonjeo galgeyo. igeo timjangnim juseyo.
choices.en: I'm heading out first. Give this to the team lead. (curt, no softening)
choices.feedback: This announces your departure and gives an order without first asking whether your coworker can help.

choices.ko: 이 서류 좀 전달해. 나 가야 돼.
choices.romanization: i seoryu jom jeondalhae. na gaya dwae.
choices.en: Pass this document along. I gotta go. (반말, ordering)
choices.feedback: Both sentences are in casual speech and sound like an order in this workplace setting.

turns.ko: 아, 네. 그 정도는 괜찮아요. 언제까지 드리면 될까요?
turns.romanization: a, ne. geu jeongdoneun gwaenchanayo. eonjekkaji deurimyeon doelkkayo?
turns.en: Oh, sure. I can do that. By when should I give it to them?

turns.prompt: Say before the 3 o'clock meeting is fine, and add a second small request to answer a call if a client phones.

choices.ko: 3시 회의 전까지만 팀장님께 전달해 주시면 돼요. 그리고 혹시 거래처에서 전화가 오면 대신 좀 받아 주실 수 있을까요?
choices.romanization: 3si hoeui jeonkkajiman timjangnimkke jeondalhae jusimyeon dwaeyo. geurigo hoksi georaecheoeseo jeonhwaga omyeon daesin jom bada jusil su isseulkkayo?
choices.en: Just pass it to the team lead before the 3 o'clock meeting. And if a client calls, could you answer it for me?
choices.feedback: 전까지만 gives a clear deadline, and the second favor is introduced again with 혹시 and a polite question.

choices.en: Before the meeting. You answer the phone too. (반말, bossy)
choices.feedback: The clipped deadline and 네가 받아 sound bossy, and the casual speech is wrong for this coworker.

choices.en: Whenever. Just deal with the phone yourself. (dismissive)
choices.feedback: 아무 때나요 is vague, and 알아서 하세요 pushes responsibility onto the coworker dismissively.

turns.ko: 전화는 제가 받을게요. 그런데 거래처 건은 제가 내용을 잘 몰라서, 메모만 남겨 둬도 될까요?
turns.romanization: jeonhwaneun jega badeulgeyo. geureonde georaecheo geoneun jega naeyongeul jal mollaseo, memoman namgyeo dwodo doelkkayo?
turns.en: I'll take the call. But I don't really know the details of the client matter, so would it be okay if I just leave a note?

turns.prompt: Graciously accept their limit, make it easy for them, and thank them sincerely.

choices.ko: 그럼요, 메모만 남겨 주셔도 충분해요. 무리한 부탁을 드려서 죄송하고, 정말 감사합니다. 다음에 꼭 보답할게요!
choices.romanization: geureomyo, memoman namgyeo jusyeodo chungbunhaeyo. murihan butageul deuryeoseo joesonghago, jeongmal gamsahamnida. daeume kkok bodapalgeyo!
choices.en: Of course, just a note is more than enough. Sorry for asking so much, and thank you so much. I'll definitely return the favor next time!
choices.feedback: This accepts the coworker's limit, lowers the burden, apologizes, and closes with sincere thanks.

choices.ko: 아니요, 꼭 통화하고 처리해 주셔야 돼요.
choices.romanization: aniyo, kkok tonghwahago cheorihae jusyeoya dwaeyo.
choices.en: No, you absolutely have to handle it on the call. (pushy, ignores their limit)
choices.feedback: 꼭 and -주셔야 돼요 ignore the coworker's reasonable limit and turn the favor into a demand.

choices.en: A note? That's kind of a problem. (ungracious)
choices.feedback: This rejects the help being offered without gratitude or an easier alternative.

turns.ko: 아니에요, 이 정도는 괜찮아요. 일 잘 보고 오세요.
turns.romanization: anieyo, i jeongdoneun gwaenchanayo. il jal bogo oseyo.
turns.en: Not at all, this much is fine. Take care of your appointment.

buddyCard.instructionKo: 부탁을 받는 직장 동료 역할을 해 주세요. 무슨 일인지와 서류를 언제까지 전달하면 되는지 물어봐 주세요. 학습자는 초급이니 공손하고 천천히 말해 주세요.

conversations.title: Opening a bank account
conversations.situation: You go to a bank in Korea to open your first account. You greet the teller, say what you need, and hand over your ID to fill out the form.
conversations.tip: At the counter, '계좌를 만들고 싶어요' or '계좌를 개설하려고 왔어요' both work. Foreigners usually need a 외국인등록증 (ARC) as 신분증.

turns.ko: 어서 오세요. 무엇을 도와드릴까요?
turns.romanization: eoseo oseyo. mueoseul dowadeurilkkayo?
turns.en: Welcome. How can I help you?

turns.prompt: Say you'd like to open a bank account.

choices.en: I'd like to open an account.
choices.feedback: -고 싶어요 states what service you want clearly and politely at the counter.

choices.en: Make me an account. (too casual/rude)
choices.feedback: The casual command 만들어 is rude to a bank employee.

choices.en: I need money. (wrong meaning)
choices.feedback: This says you need money; it does not ask to open an account.

turns.ko: 네, 신분증 좀 보여 주시겠어요?
turns.romanization: ne, sinbunjeung jom boyeo jusigesseoyo?
turns.en: Sure, could you show me your ID, please?

turns.prompt: Hand over your ID and say 'here you are'. (You only have your foreigner ID card.)

choices.en: Here's my foreigner registration card.
choices.feedback: 여기 N이요 is a concise, polite way to hand over the requested document.

choices.en: I don't have an ID. (then you can't open one)
choices.feedback: This contradicts the situation because you do have your foreigner registration card.

choices.en: My passport is at home. (unhelpful)
choices.feedback: This does not hand over the ID you have with you, so the transaction cannot continue.

turns.ko: 감사합니다. 이 신청서를 작성해 주세요.
turns.romanization: gamsahamnida. i sincheongseoreul jakseonghae juseyo.
turns.en: Thank you. Please fill out this application form.

turns.prompt: Ask where you should write your phone number on the form.

choices.en: Where should I write my phone number?
choices.feedback: 어디에 적으면 돼요? asks for the exact place on the form naturally and politely.

choices.en: I don't know the phone number. (odd)
choices.feedback: This says you do not know the number instead of asking where to write it.

choices.en: Do I write all of this? (vague)
choices.feedback: 이거 and 다 are too vague; the question must identify the phone-number field.

turns.ko: 여기 이름 옆에 적어 주시면 돼요. 체크카드도 함께 만들어 드릴까요?
turns.romanization: yeogi ireum yeope jeogeo jusimyeon dwaeyo. chekeukadeudo hamkke mandeureo deurilkkayo?
turns.en: Just write it next to your name. Shall I make you a debit card too?

turns.prompt: Say yes, and ask if there's a fee.

choices.en: Yes, please make one. Is there a fee?
choices.feedback: This accepts the card offer and follows with the practical fee question in polite speech.

choices.en: No, just the bankbook. I hate cards. (blunt)
choices.feedback: This rejects the card and does not ask about the fee; 카드 싫어요 also sounds unnecessarily blunt.

choices.en: What's a card? (unnatural here)
choices.feedback: The employee already offered a specific debit card, so this broad question is unnatural and misses the fee prompt.
