turns.ko: 카드 발급 수수료는 없어요. 통장과 카드는 잠시 후에 나옵니다.
turns.romanization: kadeu balgeup susuryoneun eopseoyo. tongjanggwa kadeuneun jamsi hue naomnida.
turns.en: There is no card issuance fee. Your bankbook and card will be ready in a moment.

buddyCard.instructionKo: 은행 창구 직원 역할을 해 주세요. 어떤 업무로 왔는지 묻고, 신분증과 신청서를 요청한 뒤 체크카드가 필요한지도 물어봐 주세요. 학습자는 초급이니 공손하고 짧게 안내해 주세요.

conversations.title: Getting a document at the district office
conversations.situation: You visit the 구청 (district office) to apply for and pick up an official document. You take a number, submit your papers, and ask when it will be ready.
conversations.tip: At a 구청 or immigration office, take a 번호표 first and wait for your number. Use '신청하다' to apply, '발급받다' to get a document issued, and '접수하다' for them processing/receiving it.

turns.ko: 안녕하세요. 번호표 뽑고 잠시 기다려 주세요.
turns.romanization: annyeonghaseyo. beonhopyo ppopgo jamsi gidaryeo juseyo.
turns.en: Hello. Please take a number and wait a moment.

turns.prompt: Ask where the number-ticket machine is.

choices.en: Where do I take a number ticket?
choices.feedback: 어디에서 뽑아요? asks for the ticket machine's location clearly and politely.

choices.en: Give me a number. (too casual/rude)
choices.feedback: 줘 is a casual command to the staff member and does not ask where the machine is.

choices.en: What's the number? (confusing)
choices.feedback: This asks what a number is, not where to take a number ticket.

turns.ko: 입구 오른쪽에 있어요. 다음 손님, 무엇을 도와드릴까요?
turns.romanization: ipgu oreunjjoge isseoyo. daeum sonnim, mueoseul dowadeurilkkayo?
turns.en: It's on the right at the entrance. Next customer, how can I help you?

turns.prompt: Say you came to apply for a certificate of residence (a document).

choices.en: I came to get a copy of my resident registration issued.
choices.feedback: Naming the document and using -으러 왔어요 tells the clerk exactly why you came.

choices.en: Give me the document, quickly. (impolite)
choices.feedback: The document is not identified, and 빨리요 makes the request sound impatient.

choices.en: Do you have documents here? (vague)
choices.feedback: 서류 is too vague, and this does not explain that you came to have one issued.

turns.ko: 네, 신분증과 신청서를 주시겠어요?
turns.romanization: ne, sinbunjeunggwa sincheongseoreul jusigesseoyo?
turns.en: Sure, could you give me your ID and the application form?

turns.prompt: Hand them over and say you've already filled out the form.

choices.en: Here you are. I filled out the form in advance.
choices.feedback: 여기 있어요 hands over both items, and 미리 작성했어요 gives the requested status clearly.

choices.en: I didn't fill it out, just give it to me. (won't work)
choices.feedback: This refuses the required form and demands the document without completing the process.

choices.en: Is this right? (too vague)
choices.feedback: 이거 does not identify the ID or form, and the sentence never says the form is complete.

turns.ko: 접수해 드렸습니다. 수수료는 천 원입니다.
turns.romanization: jeopsuhae deuryeotseumnida. susuryoneun cheon wonimnida.
turns.en: I've processed your application. The fee is 1,000 won.

turns.prompt: Pay, and ask when the document will be ready.

choices.ko: 여기요. 서류는 언제 받을 수 있을까요?
choices.romanization: yeogiyo. seoryuneun eonje badeul su isseulkkayo?
choices.en: Here you go. When will I be able to receive the document?
choices.feedback: 여기요 accompanies the payment, and -을 수 있을까요? asks the ready time politely.

choices.en: Why is it so expensive? (rude over 1,000 won)
choices.feedback: This complains about the stated fee and never asks when the document will be ready.

choices.en: Give it to me right now. (demanding)
choices.feedback: 지금 당장 주세요 is a demand and ignores the processing time.

turns.ko: 십 분 정도 걸려요. 성함을 부르면 이쪽으로 와 주세요.
turns.romanization: sip bun jeongdo geollyeoyo. seonghameul bureumyeon ijjogeuro wa juseyo.
turns.en: It takes about ten minutes. When I call your name, please come over here.

buddyCard.instructionKo: 구청 민원 창구 직원 역할을 해 주세요. 번호표를 안내하고, 필요한 서류와 신분증을 요청한 뒤 발급 시간을 알려 주세요. 학습자는 초급이니 공손하고 천천히 설명해 주세요.

conversations.title: Your Usual at the Café
conversations.situation: You walk into the café you go to every week and the owner recognizes you right away.
conversations.tip: Regular-customer small talk lives on tiny extras: order, add one small comment, then ask the owner something back. A bare 네 ends the chat before it starts.

turns.ko: 어, 오셨네요! 오늘도 같은 걸로 드릴까요?
turns.romanization: eo, osyeonneyo! oneuldo gateun geollo deurilkkayo?
turns.en: Oh, you're here! Same thing as always?

turns.prompt: Order your usual and add a small friendly comment

choices.ko: 네, 아이스 아메리카노요! 여기 커피가 제일 맛있어서요ㅎㅎ
choices.romanization: ne, aiseu amerikanoyo! yeogi keopiga jeil masisseoseoyohh
choices.en: Yes, iced americano! Your coffee is the best, that's whyㅎㅎ
choices.feedback: Orders and adds a small compliment — that extra half-sentence is what turns a transaction into small talk.

choices.en: Yes.
choices.feedback: Grammatical but a dead end. The owner opened a friendly door and you closed it in one syllable.

choices.en: I shall place an order for the identical beverage.
choices.feedback: 합니다체 plus stiff written vocabulary (동일한 음료) — sounds like a form, not a regular saying hi.

turns.ko: 아이고 감사해요ㅎㅎ 오늘 진짜 덥죠? 밖에 난리예요.
turns.romanization: aigo gamsahaeyohh oneul jinjja deopjyo? bakke nalliyeyo.
turns.en: Aw, thank youㅎㅎ It's really hot today, right? It's wild outside.

turns.prompt: Agree about the heat and ask the owner something back

choices.ko: 그러니까요, 나오자마자 땀났어요. 사장님은 오늘 바쁘셨어요?
choices.romanization: geureonikkayo, naojamaja ttamnasseoyo. sajangnimeun oneul bappeusyeosseoyo?
choices.en: Right? I started sweating the second I stepped out. Were you busy today?
choices.feedback: 그러니까요 agrees, one concrete detail (땀났어요) proves you mean it, and the question back makes it two-way.

choices.en: Yes, it is hot.
choices.feedback: Correct Korean, but flat and one-way — the owner has to do all the work of keeping this going.

choices.ko: 오늘 최고 기온이 삼십사 도까지 올라간다고 합니다.
choices.romanization: oneul choego gioni samsipsa dokkaji ollagandago hamnida.
choices.en: Today's high is reported to reach thirty-four degrees.
choices.feedback: You answered like a weather forecast instead of a person. Reporting facts isn't reacting.

turns.ko: 아침엔 좀 바빴는데 지금은 한가해요. 저는 이 시간이 제일 좋아요.
turns.romanization: achimen jom bappanneunde jigeumeun hangahaeyo. jeoneun i sigani jeil joayo.
turns.en: Mornings get busy, but it's quiet now. This is my favorite time of day.

turns.prompt: Say you like this time too and give a reason

choices.ko: 저도 이 시간이 좋아요. 조용해서 책 읽기 딱이에요.
choices.romanization: jeodo i sigani joayo. joyonghaeseo chaek ilkgi ttagieyo.
choices.en: I like this time too. It's quiet, so it's perfect for reading.
choices.feedback: 저도 finds common ground, and the reason (조용해서) gives the owner something to keep talking about.

choices.en: I see.
choices.feedback: Polite but empty. 그렇군요 acknowledges without offering anything — the conversation stalls right here.

choices.en: So business must be slow, then?
choices.feedback: Grammatical, but it turns a warm remark into a jab at their business. Read 한가해요 as relief, not a complaint.

turns.ko: 맞아요ㅎㅎ 편하게 계시다 가세요. 커피 나오면 불러 드릴게요.
turns.romanization: majayohh pyeonhage gyesida gaseyo. keopi naomyeon bulleo deurilgeyo.
turns.en: Exactlyㅎㅎ Make yourself comfortable. I'll call you when the coffee's ready.

turns.prompt: Close the chat warmly

choices.en: Sure, thank you! I'll enjoy itㅎㅎ
choices.feedback: Short, warm, and 잘 마실게요 is the natural little sign-off Koreans use when someone hands them a drink.

choices.en: Yeah, got it.
choices.feedback: This is 반말. Even with a friendly owner you know well, dropping to 반말 first sounds presumptuous — stay in 해요체.

choices.ko: 커피가 몇 분 후에 나오는지 정확히 알려 주시겠습니까?
choices.romanization: keopiga myeot bun hue naoneunji jeonghwaki allyeo jusigetseumnikka?
choices.en: Could you tell me precisely how many minutes until the coffee is ready?
choices.feedback: Over-formal and oddly demanding for a café you visit weekly — it makes a kind offer sound like a complaint.

buddyCard.instructionKo: 학습자가 매주 오는 단골인 카페 사장님 역할을 해 주세요. 반갑게 알아보고 늘 마시던 걸로 시킬지 물어본 다음, 날씨나 오늘 손님이 많았는지 같은 가벼운 이야기를 건네 주세요. 학습자는 초급이니 해요체로 짧고 천천히 말해 주세요.

conversations.title: Language Exchange: First Meeting
conversations.situation: You meet your new language exchange partner at a café for the very first time.
conversations.tip: First meetings run on 해요체 both ways. Answer, add one honest detail, then hand the question back (…씨는요?) — that loop is what makes a second meeting happen.

turns.ko: 안녕하세요! 저 지수예요. 만나서 반가워요ㅎㅎ
turns.romanization: annyeonghaseyo! jeo jisuyeyo. mannaseo bangawoyohh
turns.en: Hi! I'm Jisu. Nice to meet youㅎㅎ

turns.prompt: Introduce yourself and greet them back

choices.ko: 안녕하세요, 저는 크리스예요! 저도 반가워요. 오래 기다리셨어요?
choices.romanization: annyeonghaseyo, jeoneun keuriseuyeyo! jeodo bangawoyo. orae gidarisyeosseoyo?
choices.en: Hi, I'm Chris! Nice to meet you too. Did you wait long?
choices.feedback: Name, matching greeting, and a small caring question — 해요체 like this is exactly the register between new peers.

choices.en: Good day. I am called Chris.
choices.feedback: 합니다체 is fine on a stage or in a job interview, not across a café table. It puts distance where you want warmth.

choices.en: Yes, hello.
choices.feedback: You never said your name. They introduced themselves and got almost nothing back — an awkward start.

turns.ko: 아니에요, 저도 방금 왔어요. 한국어 공부한 지 얼마나 됐어요?
turns.romanization: anieyo, jeodo banggeum wasseoyo. hangugeo gongbuhan ji eolmana dwaesseoyo?
turns.en: Not at all, I just got here too. How long have you been studying Korean?

turns.prompt: Answer how long, then ask about their English

choices.ko: 한 육 개월 됐어요. 아직 어려운데 재밌어요! 지수 씨는 영어 오래 했어요?
choices.romanization: han yuk gaewol dwaesseoyo. ajik eoryeounde jaemisseoyo! jisu ssineun yeongeo orae haesseoyo?
choices.en: About six months. Still hard, but fun! Jisu, have you studied English long?
choices.feedback: 한 육 개월 (about six months) sounds relaxed, the honest 어려운데 재밌어요 invites empathy, and the bounce-back keeps it balanced.

choices.en: Six months.
choices.feedback: A bare fact. True, polite, and the conversation now has nowhere to go.

choices.ko: 저는 한국어를 육 개월 동안 학습하였습니다.
choices.romanization: jeoneun hangugeoreul yuk gaewol dongan hakseupayeotseumnida.
choices.en: I have been engaged in the study of the Korean language for six months.
choices.feedback: 학습하였습니다 is textbook written Korean. Nobody says this out loud to someone they just met over coffee.

turns.ko: 저는 학교 때부터 했는데 말하기는 아직 자신 없어요ㅠㅠ
turns.romanization: jeoneun hakgyo ttaebuteo haenneunde malhagineun ajik jasin eopseoyoyuyu
turns.en: Since school, but I'm still not confident speakingㅠㅠ

turns.prompt: Relate to their nerves instead of advising them

choices.ko: 저도 똑같아요! 말할 때 제일 떨려요. 그래서 이런 만남이 좋은 것 같아요.
choices.romanization: jeodo ttokgatayo! malhal ttae jeil tteollyeoyo. geuraeseo ireon mannami joeun geot gatayo.
choices.en: Same here! Speaking makes me the most nervous. That's why meetups like this are good.
choices.feedback: 저도 똑같아요 turns their weak spot into shared ground, and it quietly explains why you're both sitting here.

choices.en: Then you'll have to study harder.
choices.feedback: Grammatical, but they were being vulnerable, not asking for advice. This lands as a lecture.

choices.en: Ah, I see.
choices.feedback: They just admitted something a bit embarrassing and you gave them nothing back. React first, always.

turns.ko: 맞아요ㅎㅎ 그럼 우리 반은 한국어, 반은 영어로 할까요?
turns.romanization: majayohh geureom uri baneun hangugeo, baneun yeongeoro halkkayo?
turns.en: Rightㅎㅎ So should we do half Korean, half English?

turns.prompt: Agree to the plan and set up a next meeting

choices.ko: 좋아요! 삼십 분씩 나눠서 해요. 다음 주에도 이 시간에 만날 수 있어요?
choices.romanization: joayo! samsip bunssing nanwoseo haeyo. daeum juedo i sigane mannal su isseoyo?
choices.en: Sounds good! Let's split it thirty minutes each. Can we meet at this time next week too?
choices.feedback: Says yes, makes it concrete (삼십 분씩), then proposes a next time — this is how a first meeting becomes a routine.

choices.en: Yes, let's proceed that way.
choices.feedback: 하시죠 sounds like a manager closing a meeting. Correct grammar, wrong power dynamic between equals.

choices.en: I'd like to do it in English only.
choices.feedback: Perfectly grammatical and completely misses the point — a language exchange only works if both sides get practice.

turns.ko: 네 좋아요! 그럼 다음 주 같은 시간에 여기서 봐요ㅎㅎ
turns.romanization: ne joayo! geureom daeum ju gateun sigane yeogiseo bwayohh
turns.en: Great! Then see you here at the same time next weekㅎㅎ

buddyCard.instructionKo: 오늘 처음 만난 언어교환 파트너 역할을 해 주세요. 이름을 먼저 밝히고 한국어를 얼마나 공부했는지 물어본 뒤, 한국어와 영어를 반씩 하자고 제안하고 다음에 또 만나자고 해 주세요. 존댓말 중에서도 딱딱한 합니다체 말고 편한 해요체로 말해 주세요.
buddyCard.reactionKo: 오, 육 개월밖에 안 됐는데 잘하시는데요!

conversations.title: Lunch with a Coworker
conversations.situation: You grab lunch near the office with a coworker and make easy small talk.
conversations.tip: Coworker lunch talk stays light: give a real answer, keep it short, and pass the question back. Never judge what they say they enjoy.

turns.ko: 오늘 점심 뭐 드실래요? 여기 김치찌개 괜찮아요.
turns.romanization: oneul jeomsim mwo deusillaeyo? yeogi gimchijjigae gwaenchanayo.
turns.en: What do you want for lunch? The kimchi jjigae here is good.

turns.prompt: Go along with their suggestion warmly

choices.ko: 오 좋아요, 저 김치찌개 좋아해요. 그걸로 할게요!
choices.romanization: o joayo, jeo gimchijjigae joahaeyo. geugeollo halgeyo!
choices.en: Oh nice, I love kimchi jjigae. I'll go with that!
choices.feedback: Takes the suggestion and shows you actually want it — 그걸로 할게요 is the everyday way to lock in an order.

choices.en: Anything is fine with me.
choices.feedback: 합니다체 plus total indifference. It reads as 'I don't care', which is a cold answer to a friendly recommendation.

choices.ko: 그건 제가 결정할 사항이 아닌 것 같아요.
choices.romanization: geugeon jega gyeoljeonghal sahangi anin geot gatayo.
choices.en: I don't think that's a matter for me to decide.
choices.feedback: Grammatical, but treating a lunch order like a business decision is oddly distant.

turns.ko: 그럼 두 개 시킬게요. 참, 주말에 뭐 했어요?
turns.romanization: geureom du gae sikilgeyo. cham, jumare mwo haesseoyo?
turns.en: I'll order two then. Oh, what did you do this weekend?

turns.prompt: Say what you did and ask about their weekend

choices.ko: 친구랑 한강 갔어요! 날씨 좋아서 좋더라고요. 지수 씨는요?
choices.romanization: chingurang hangang gasseoyo! nalssi joaseo joteoragoyo. jisu ssineunyo?
choices.en: I went to the Han River with a friend! The weather was great. How about you?
choices.feedback: One concrete thing, one feeling (좋더라고요), then …씨는요? — the shortest way to hand the turn back.

choices.en: I just rested.
choices.feedback: A safe answer that gives them nothing to ask about. Add one detail or a question back.

choices.en: I shall now report on my weekend activities.
choices.feedback: This is presentation Korean. Announcing that you're about to answer sounds like a work briefing, not lunch.

turns.ko: 저는 그냥 집에서 밀린 드라마 봤어요ㅎㅎ 요즘 뭐 재밌는 거 있어요?
turns.romanization: jeoneun geunyang jibeseo millin deurama bwasseoyohh yojeum mwo jaeminneun geo isseoyo?
turns.en: I just caught up on dramas at homeㅎㅎ Anything fun going on for you these days?

turns.prompt: Share what you're into and ask about their drama

choices.ko: 요즘 클라이밍 배워요. 힘든데 재밌어요ㅎㅎ 드라마 뭐 보셨어요?
choices.romanization: yojeum keullaiming baewoyo. himdeunde jaemisseoyohh deurama mwo bosyeosseoyo?
choices.en: I'm learning climbing these days. Tough but funㅎㅎ Which drama did you watch?
choices.feedback: Answers with something specific, then picks up the thing they mentioned. Reusing their topic shows you were listening.

choices.en: Nothing in particular.
choices.feedback: A polite door slam. They shared theirs and asked — give them something, even something small.

choices.ko: 드라마 보는 건 시간 낭비 아니에요?
choices.romanization: deurama boneun geon sigan nangbi anieyo?
choices.en: Isn't watching dramas a waste of time?
choices.feedback: Grammatical, but you just criticized how they spend their weekend. That ends coworker small talk fast.

turns.ko: 오 클라이밍이요? 저도 한번 해 보고 싶었는데요!
turns.romanization: o keullaimingiyo? jeodo hanbeon hae bogo sipeonneundeyo!
turns.en: Oh, climbing? I've been wanting to try that!

turns.prompt: Invite them along and lower the barrier

choices.ko: 그럼 언제 같이 가요! 초보자도 다 하니까 괜찮아요.
choices.romanization: geureom eonje gachi gayo! chobojado da hanikka gwaenchanayo.
choices.en: Then let's go together sometime! Beginners do it all the time, so it's fine.
choices.feedback: 같이 가요 turns interest into a real invitation, and 초보자도 다 하니까 removes the excuse to say no.

choices.en: Yeah, it's fun.
choices.feedback: They basically invited themselves and you didn't catch it. A clear opening went unanswered.

choices.en: I respectfully request that you go climbing with me.
choices.feedback: Grammatical and wildly over-formal — it makes a casual lunch invite sound like an official letter.

buddyCard.instructionKo: 학습자와 같이 점심을 먹으러 나온 회사 동료 역할을 해 주세요. 메뉴를 추천하고 주말에 뭐 했는지, 요즘 재밌는 게 있는지 가볍게 물어봐 주세요. 회사 밖이니까 편한 해요체로 짧게 말해 주세요.

conversations.title: Neighbor in the Elevator
conversations.situation: You run into a neighbor from your building in the elevator on the way up.
conversations.tip: An elevator ride is thirty seconds long. Greet, add one light comment, and close — anything longer or more formal feels heavy for the space.

turns.ko: 아, 안녕하세요! 몇 층 누를까요?
turns.romanization: a, annyeonghaseyo! myeot cheung nureulkkayo?
turns.en: Oh, hello! Which floor should I press?

turns.prompt: Greet back and answer the floor

choices.en: Hello! Twelfth floor, thank youㅎㅎ
choices.feedback: Greeting, floor, thanks — the whole elevator exchange in one breath. This is exactly the right size.

choices.en: Twelfth floor.
choices.feedback: You skipped both the greeting and the thanks. Grammatical, but it comes off as brusque to a neighbor doing you a favor.

choices.ko: 십이 층 버튼을 눌러 주시기 바랍니다.
choices.romanization: sibi cheung beoteuneul nulleo jusigi baramnida.
choices.en: Kindly press the button for the twelfth floor.
choices.feedback: 주시기 바랍니다 belongs in an announcement. Answering a neighbor's small kindness this formally sounds cold.

turns.ko: 네네. 오늘 밖에 많이 춥죠? 장 보고 오시나 봐요.
turns.romanization: nene. oneul bakke mani chupjyo? jang bogo osina bwayo.
turns.en: Sure. It's really cold out today, isn't it? Looks like you've been grocery shopping.

turns.prompt: Agree about the cold and add a light comment about your bags

choices.ko: 네, 진짜 춥더라고요. 마트 갔다가 너무 많이 샀어요ㅎㅎ
choices.romanization: ne, jinjja chupdeoragoyo. mateu gatdaga neomu mani sasseoyohh
choices.en: Yeah, it was really cold. I went to the mart and bought way too muchㅎㅎ
choices.feedback: Agrees, then makes a tiny joke at your own expense — light, warm, and over in one line.

choices.en: Yes, it is cold.
choices.feedback: 합니다체 and nothing else. It's correct, but it makes the last ten floors feel very long.

choices.ko: 오늘 최저 기온은 영하 오 도입니다.
choices.romanization: oneul choejeo gioneun yeongha o doimnida.
choices.en: Today's low is minus five degrees.
choices.feedback: Reciting numbers instead of reacting. They were being friendly, not asking for data.

turns.ko: 무거워 보여요ㅎㅎ 하나 들어 드릴까요?
turns.romanization: mugeowo boyeoyohh hana deureo deurilkkayo?
turns.en: Looks heavyㅎㅎ Want me to carry one?

turns.prompt: Turn down the offer without making it awkward

choices.en: Oh no, I'm fine! I'll just take the thoughtㅎㅎ Thank you.
choices.feedback: 마음만 받을게요 is the set phrase for declining a kind offer while still accepting the kindness — perfect elevator-sized close.

choices.en: Sure, please carry one.
choices.feedback: Grammatical, but a passing courtesy for a short ride isn't really meant to be taken up. It puts your neighbor on the spot.

choices.en: That is fine.
choices.feedback: Declines, but so curtly it sounds like you're brushing them off. Soften it and thank them.

turns.ko: 네ㅎㅎ 그럼 조심히 들어가세요!
turns.romanization: nehh geureom josimhi deureogaseyo!
turns.en: Okayㅎㅎ Get home safe, then!

buddyCard.instructionKo: 같은 건물에 사는 이웃 역할을 해 주세요. 엘리베이터에서 마주쳐서 몇 층인지 물어보고, 날씨나 들고 있는 짐 이야기를 한마디만 건넨 다음 인사하고 마무리해 주세요. 엘리베이터 안이라 대화가 짧으니 한 문장씩만 짧게 말해 주세요.

conversations.title: At the Hair Salon
conversations.situation: You're at a hair salon telling the stylist what you want, and she chats with you while she cuts.
conversations.tip: Keep your request short and concrete (얼마나 / 어디를), then react to the stylist's small talk instead of just answering. 해요체 is exactly right here — friendly but polite, no need for 합니다체.

turns.ko: 안녕하세요~ 오늘 어떻게 해 드릴까요?
turns.romanization: annyeonghaseyo~ oneul eotteoke hae deurilkkayo?
turns.en: Hello~ What would you like done today?

turns.prompt: Say what you want, simply

choices.ko: 안녕하세요. 너무 짧지 않게 조금만 잘라 주세요.
choices.romanization: annyeonghaseyo. neomu jjalbji anke jogeumman jalla juseyo.
choices.en: Hello. Just a little trim, not too short please.
choices.feedback: Short, concrete, and 해요체 — 조금만 잘라 주세요 gives the stylist exactly what she needs without complicated vocabulary.

choices.ko: 제 두발을 단정하게 정리해 주시기 바랍니다.
choices.romanization: je dubareul danjeonghage jeongnihae jusigi baramnida.
choices.en: I request that you tidy up my hair neatly.
choices.feedback: Grammatical, but 두발 and -주시기 바랍니다 belong on an official notice. In a salon it sounds like you're filing paperwork.

choices.en: Anything is fine with me.
choices.feedback: Polite but useless here — she asked a real question, and 아무거나 leaves her guessing. Give one specific detail instead.

turns.ko: 네~ 그럼 이 정도 길이면 괜찮을까요?
turns.romanization: ne~ geureom i jeongdo girimyeon gwaenchaneulkkayo?
turns.en: Sure~ So would about this length be okay?

turns.prompt: Confirm and add one small request

choices.ko: 네, 딱 좋아요. 옆머리도 조금 다듬어 주세요.
choices.romanization: ne, ttak joayo. yeommeorido jogeum dadeumeo juseyo.
choices.en: Yes, that's just right. Could you tidy up the sides a bit too?
choices.feedback: 네, 딱 좋아요 confirms clearly, and adding 옆머리도 조금 다듬어 주세요 is the natural moment to ask for one more thing.

choices.en: Yes.
choices.feedback: Correct, but a bare 네 ends the exchange. She's checking with you — a one-word answer makes her guess whether you're actually happy.

choices.en: Please judge the length however you see fit.
choices.feedback: Grammatical, but handing the whole decision back sounds distant — and it's how people end up unhappy with their haircut.

turns.ko: 한국말 잘하시네요! 한국에 오래 사셨어요?
turns.romanization: hangungmal jalhasineyo! hanguge orae sasyeosseoyo?
turns.en: Your Korean is good! Have you lived in Korea long?

turns.prompt: Answer and keep the chat going

choices.ko: 아 아직 일 년밖에 안 됐어요ㅎㅎ 여기 오래 하셨어요?
choices.romanization: a ajik il nyeonbakke an dwaesseoyohh yeogi orae hasyeosseoyo?
choices.en: Ah it's only been a year ㅎㅎ Have you worked here long?
choices.feedback: Deflects the compliment lightly, then bounces a question back — that's what turns small talk into a real conversation. ㅎㅎ softens 해요체 nicely.

choices.en: It's been a year.
choices.feedback: Grammatical and polite, but it answers and stops. She opened the door to chat; give her something to reply to.

choices.ko: 한국에 거주한 지 일 년이 경과하였습니다.
choices.romanization: hanguge geojuhan ji il nyeoni gyeonggwahayeotseumnida.
choices.en: One year has elapsed since I took up residence in Korea.
choices.feedback: Textbook 합니다체 with 거주하다 and 경과하다 — reads like a visa form. Casual salon chat wants 일 년 됐어요.

turns.ko: 다 됐어요! 어떠세요, 마음에 드세요?
turns.romanization: da dwaesseoyo! eotteoseyo, maeume deuseyo?
turns.en: All done! How is it, do you like it?

turns.prompt: Say you like it and close warmly

choices.ko: 우와 마음에 들어요! 감사합니다, 다음에 또 올게요.
choices.romanization: uwa maeume deureoyo! gamsahamnida, daeume tto olgeyo.
choices.en: Wow, I love it! Thank you, I'll come again next time.
choices.feedback: A quick reaction (우와) plus 또 올게요 is the standard warm way to leave a salon — it thanks her and signals you'd come back.

choices.en: Yes, I like it.
choices.feedback: Fine grammar, flat delivery. After she's worked on you for an hour, a flat 네 lands as lukewarm.

choices.ko: 결과에 대해서 만족한다고 말씀드릴 수 있습니다.
choices.romanization: gyeolgwae daehaeseo manjokandago malsseumdeuril su itseumnida.
choices.en: I can state that I am satisfied with the result.
choices.feedback: Grammatical but sounds like a customer survey response. Stick to plain 해요체: 마음에 들어요.

buddyCard.instructionKo: 머리를 잘라 주는 미용사 역할을 해 주세요. 어떻게 잘라 드릴지 묻고, 자르는 동안 한국말 잘한다는 칭찬이나 날씨 같은 가벼운 수다를 걸어 주세요. 학습자는 초급이니 해요체로 짧고 천천히 말해 주세요.

conversations.title: Chatting in the Taxi
conversations.situation: You get in a taxi, tell the driver where you're going, and make small talk on the way.
conversations.tip: Destination first, in one clean line: 「(장소)로 가 주세요」. After that, 해요체 keeps things friendly — the driver may sound warm and chatty, but you never need to switch registers.

turns.ko: 어서 오세요~ 어디로 모실까요?
turns.romanization: eoseo oseyo~ eodiro mosilkkayo?
turns.en: Welcome~ Where shall I take you?

turns.prompt: Give your destination

choices.en: Hello, to Seoul Station please.
choices.feedback: The standard formula: 장소 + 로 가 주세요. Clear, polite, and it's the first thing every driver is waiting to hear.

choices.en: I request operation as far as Seoul Station.
choices.feedback: Grammatical, but 운행 is what a bus company says. To a driver it sounds oddly official — 가 주세요 is what people actually say.

choices.en: Do you happen to know Seoul Station?
choices.feedback: Perfectly grammatical, but asking a taxi driver if he knows Seoul Station sounds like you doubt him. Just name the place.

turns.ko: 네, 서울역이요. 지금 길이 좀 막히는데 괜찮으세요?
turns.romanization: ne, seouryeogiyo. jigeum giri jom makineunde gwaenchaneuseyo?
turns.en: Okay, Seoul Station. Traffic's a bit heavy right now — is that alright?

turns.prompt: Tell him it's fine

choices.ko: 네 괜찮아요. 시간 넉넉해서 천천히 가도 돼요.
choices.romanization: ne gwaenchanayo. sigan neongneokaeseo cheoncheonhi gado dwaeyo.
choices.en: Yeah it's fine. I have plenty of time, so we can take it slow.
choices.feedback: Answers the question and explains why — 시간 넉넉해요 tells him he doesn't have to rush, which is the real information he wants.

choices.en: How bad is the traffic? I really can't be late.
choices.feedback: Grammatical, but he asked whether you're okay with it and you've turned it into pressure. If you're not in a hurry, don't create one.

choices.en: I shall bear the traffic conditions myself.
choices.feedback: Stiff 합니다체 with 감수하다 — it's a courtroom sentence in a taxi. 괜찮아요 does the whole job.

turns.ko: 한국말 잘하시네요~ 한국에 여행 오셨어요?
turns.romanization: hangungmal jalhasineyo~ hanguge yeohaeng osyeosseoyo?
turns.en: Your Korean is good~ Are you visiting Korea?

turns.prompt: Answer and show interest back

choices.ko: 아니요, 여기 살아요. 기사님은 이 일 오래 하셨어요?
choices.romanization: aniyo, yeogi sarayo. gisanimeun i il orae hasyeosseoyo?
choices.en: No, I live here. Have you been driving long?
choices.feedback: Corrects the guess and bounces a question back with 기사님 — drivers love this, and it turns the ride into a real conversation.

choices.en: No, it's not travel.
choices.feedback: Grammatical but a dead end. He offered friendly small talk; a bare correction shuts it down.

choices.ko: 본인은 관광 목적으로 방문한 것이 아닙니다.
choices.romanization: bonineun gwangwang mokjeogeuro bangmunhan geosi animnida.
choices.en: I have not visited for tourism purposes.
choices.feedback: Grammatical, but 본인 and 방문 목적 sound like immigration control. Warm chat needs warm 해요체.

turns.ko: 다 왔어요. 여기 앞에 세워 드릴게요. 만이천 원이에요.
turns.romanization: da wasseoyo. yeogi ape sewo deurilgeyo. manicheon wonieyo.
turns.en: Here we are. I'll pull over up front. That'll be 12,000 won.

turns.prompt: Pay and say goodbye

choices.en: I'll pay by card. Thank you, drive safely!
choices.feedback: 카드로 할게요 handles payment in three words, and 안전 운전하세요 is the classic warm goodbye to a driver.

choices.en: Yeah, card.
choices.feedback: Grammatical and not rude, but after a friendly chat it lands cold. A quick 감사합니다 costs nothing.

choices.ko: 요금 만이천 원을 카드로 결제하도록 하겠습니다.
choices.romanization: yogeum manicheon woneul kadeuro gyeoljehadoro kagetseumnida.
choices.en: I shall proceed to settle the fare of 12,000 won by card.
choices.feedback: Grammatical but 결제하도록 하겠습니다 is bank-teller language. Say 카드로 할게요.

buddyCard.instructionKo: 손님을 태우고 서울역까지 가는 택시 기사님 역할을 해 주세요. 목적지를 묻고, 길이 막힌다는 이야기나 한국에 왜 왔는지 같은 짧은 수다를 걸어 주세요. 반말은 쓰지 마시고 친근한 해요체로 천천히 말해 주세요.

conversations.title: Small Talk at the Gym
conversations.situation: You chat with the person next to you before and after a workout class at your gym.
conversations.tip: Gym strangers bond over shared suffering. React honestly (힘들었어요ㅠㅠ), then ask something back — 해요체 with a ㅋㅋ or ㅎㅎ is the perfect register with someone you've just met.

turns.ko: 안녕하세요~ 여기 처음 오셨어요?
turns.romanization: annyeonghaseyo~ yeogi cheoeum osyeosseoyo?
turns.en: Hi~ Is this your first time here?

turns.prompt: Say it's your first time and ask about them

choices.ko: 네, 오늘 처음 왔어요ㅎㅎ 여기 자주 오세요?
choices.romanization: ne, oneul cheoeum wasseoyohh yeogi jaju oseyo?
choices.en: Yeah, today's my first time ㅎㅎ Do you come here often?
choices.feedback: Answers, softens it with ㅎㅎ, and immediately asks back — three seconds of work that opens a whole conversation.

choices.en: Yes, it's my first time.
choices.feedback: Grammatical and polite, but it stops dead. They reached out first; give them a thread to pull.

choices.en: I have visited this facility for the first time as of today.
choices.feedback: Grammatical, but 본 시설 and 금일 belong in a report. Nobody talks like this in workout clothes.

turns.ko: 저는 일주일에 세 번 와요. 이 수업 좀 힘들어요ㅋㅋ
turns.romanization: jeoneun iljuire se beon wayo. i sueop jom himdeureoyokk
turns.en: I come three times a week. This class is kinda tough ㅋㅋ

turns.prompt: React to the warning

choices.ko: 아 진짜요? 그럼 저 오늘 큰일 났네요ㅋㅋ
choices.romanization: a jinjjayo? geureom jeo oneul keunil nanneyokk
choices.en: Oh really? Then I'm in trouble today ㅋㅋ
choices.feedback: 아 진짜요? reacts before adding anything, and the joke matches their ㅋㅋ. Matching someone's energy is half of small talk.

choices.en: I like working out, so I'm fine.
choices.feedback: Grammatical, but brushing off their warning reads as bragging. They were being friendly, not testing you.

choices.en: Is the difficulty level of the class relatively high?
choices.feedback: Grammatical, but 해당 수업 and 편입니까 sound like an interview question. They just told you it's hard.

turns.ko: 수고하셨어요~ 어땠어요? 많이 힘들었죠?
turns.romanization: sugohasyeosseoyo~ eottaesseoyo? mani himdeureotjyo?
turns.en: Good work~ How was it? Pretty tough, right?

turns.prompt: Admit it was hard, keep it light

choices.en: It was seriously hard ㅠㅠ My legs are shaking right now ㅋㅋ
choices.feedback: Agreeing with -죠? and adding one concrete detail (다리가 후들거려요) is what makes it funny instead of just polite.

choices.en: Yes, it was a bit hard.
choices.feedback: Grammatical, but 조금 downplays the shared struggle they're inviting you to bond over. Lean in a little.

choices.en: I believe the intensity of the exercise was appropriate.
choices.feedback: Grammatical, but that's feedback for the instructor, not a reply to a sweaty classmate. 해요체 and a real reaction.

turns.ko: 그쵸ㅋㅋ 저도 처음엔 그랬어요. 다음 주에도 오세요?
turns.romanization: geuchyokk jeodo cheoeumen geuraesseoyo. daeum juedo oseyo?
turns.en: Right? ㅋㅋ I was like that at first too. Are you coming next week too?

turns.prompt: Say yes and close it out

choices.ko: 네 또 올게요! 다음에 또 봬요~
choices.romanization: ne tto olgeyo! daeume tto bwaeyo~
choices.en: Yeah, I'll come again! See you next time~
choices.feedback: 또 봬요 is the standard warm sign-off with someone you'll run into again — it says you'd be happy to talk more.

choices.en: Yes, I'll come.
choices.feedback: Grammatical, but no goodbye at all. After a friendly chat, ending without 또 봬요 feels like walking off mid-sentence.

choices.ko: 다음 주 참석 여부는 추후에 알려 드리겠습니다.
choices.romanization: daeum ju chamseok yeobuneun chuhue allyeo deurigetseumnida.
choices.en: I will inform you of my attendance next week at a later date.
choices.feedback: Grammatical, but 참석 여부 turns a friendly question into a scheduling matter. Just say 네, 또 올게요.

buddyCard.instructionKo: 운동 클래스에서 옆자리에 있는 사람 역할을 해 주세요. 수업 전에는 처음 왔냐고 묻고, 수업이 끝난 뒤에는 힘들었죠 하고 물어봐 주세요. 학습자가 편하게 대답하도록 해요체로 가볍게 말해 주세요.

conversations.title: Meeting a Friend's Parents
conversations.situation: You visit your Korean friend's home for the first time and greet his mother.
conversations.tip: This is the one place to lean formal. Stay in 해요체 overall, but keep the fixed 합니다체 set-pieces intact — 처음 뵙겠습니다 / 감사합니다 / 잘 먹겠습니다. They're frozen ritual phrases, not a full register switch, so mixing them into 해요체 is exactly what Koreans do with a friend's parents.

turns.ko: 어서 와요~ 민수 친구죠? 반가워요.
turns.romanization: eoseo wayo~ minsu chingujyo? bangawoyo.
turns.en: Come on in~ You're Minsu's friend, right? Nice to meet you.

turns.prompt: Greet her properly and introduce yourself

choices.ko: 안녕하세요, 처음 뵙겠습니다. 민수 친구 제임스예요.
choices.romanization: annyeonghaseyo, cheoeum boepgetseumnida. minsu chingu jeimseuyeyo.
choices.en: Hello, it's nice to meet you. I'm James, Minsu's friend.
choices.feedback: 처음 뵙겠습니다 is a fixed first-meeting phrase — you keep it as-is, then drop back into 해요체 for the introduction. That mix is the real target register here.

choices.en: Hi~ I'm Minsu's friend. Nice to meet you!
choices.feedback: Grammatical 해요체, and fine with someone your age — but 반가워요 back to a friend's mother is too level. First greeting to a parent needs 처음 뵙겠습니다.

choices.en: Good day. I am James, the companion of Minsu.
choices.feedback: Grammatical, but 본인 and 친우 in full 합니다체 sound like a news anchor. Formal set phrases yes, formal everything no.

turns.ko: 어머, 한국말 잘하네요. 어느 나라에서 왔어요?
turns.romanization: eomeo, hangungmal jalhaneyo. eoneu naraeseo wasseoyo?
turns.en: Oh my, your Korean is good. What country are you from?

turns.prompt: Give a short self-introduction

choices.ko: 미국에서 왔어요. 한국에 온 지 육 개월 됐어요.
choices.romanization: migugeseo wasseoyo. hanguge on ji yuk gaewol dwaesseoyo.
choices.en: I'm from the U.S. It's been six months since I came to Korea.
choices.feedback: Two short 해요체 sentences: where you're from plus how long you've been here. That second detail is what she's really curious about.

choices.en: The U.S.
choices.feedback: Not wrong, but a one-word answer to a parent making an effort feels closed off. Add one sentence.

choices.ko: 저는 미국 국적을 보유하고 있으며 육 개월 전에 입국하였습니다.
choices.romanization: jeoneun miguk gukjeogeul boyuhago isseumyeo yuk gaewol jeone ipgukayeotseumnida.
choices.en: I hold U.S. nationality and entered the country six months ago.
choices.feedback: Grammatical, but 국적 보유 and 입국하였습니다 are airport-immigration words. Warm formality, not bureaucratic formality.

turns.ko: 밥은 먹었어요? 여기 앉아요. 많이 차렸어요.
turns.romanization: babeun meogeosseoyo? yeogi anjayo. mani charyeosseoyo.
turns.en: Have you eaten? Sit here. I made a lot.

turns.prompt: Thank her before eating

choices.ko: 잘 먹겠습니다. 이렇게 준비해 주셔서 감사합니다.
choices.romanization: jal meokgetseumnida. ireoke junbihae jusyeoseo gamsahamnida.
choices.en: Thank you for the food. Thank you for going to all this trouble.
choices.feedback: 잘 먹겠습니다 is fixed — nobody says 잘 먹을게요 to a friend's mother. Pairing it with 감사합니다 is the expected move before you touch the food.

choices.en: Okay, I'll eat well. Thanks.
choices.feedback: Grammatical, but 잘 먹을게요 and 고마워요 are what you'd say to a friend. To a parent who cooked for you, the frozen forms 잘 먹겠습니다 / 감사합니다 are the ones that land.

choices.ko: 음식을 많이 준비하셨네요. 다 먹을 수 있을까요?
choices.romanization: eumsigeul mani junbihasyeonneyo. da meogeul su isseulkkayo?
choices.en: You've prepared a lot of food. Will I be able to finish it all?
choices.feedback: Grammatical, and it's a joke a Korean might make — but as a first-time guest it reads as commenting on her cooking instead of thanking her.

turns.ko: 많이 먹어요~ 앞으로 자주 놀러 와요.
turns.romanization: mani meogeoyo~ apeuro jaju nolleo wayo.
turns.en: Eat lots~ Come visit often from now on.

turns.prompt: Close warmly and accept the invitation

choices.ko: 네, 정말 맛있게 잘 먹었습니다. 또 인사드릴게요.
choices.romanization: ne, jeongmal masitge jal meogeotseumnida. tto insadeurilgeyo.
choices.en: Yes, it was really delicious, thank you. I'll come pay my respects again.
choices.feedback: 잘 먹었습니다 closes the meal ritual that 잘 먹겠습니다 opened, and 인사드릴게요 accepts her invitation with the humble verb 드리다 — warm, not stiff.

choices.en: Yeah, it was tasty. I'll come again.
choices.feedback: Grammatical 해요체 and not rude — just level. After a meal a parent cooked for you, 잘 먹었습니다 is the phrase everyone expects to hear.

choices.ko: 차후 방문 일정을 조율하여 다시 연락드리겠습니다.
choices.romanization: chahu bangmun iljeongeul joyulhayeo dasi yeollakdeurigetseumnida.
choices.en: I will coordinate a future visit schedule and contact you again.
choices.feedback: Grammatical, but 일정을 조율하여 turns her warm invitation into a business appointment. Formal doesn't mean corporate.

buddyCard.instructionKo: 집에 처음 놀러 온 아들 친구를 맞이하는 어머니 역할을 해 주세요. 반갑게 인사하고, 어느 나라에서 왔는지 묻고, 밥 먹으라고 권해 주세요. 학습자가 처음 뵙겠습니다, 잘 먹겠습니다 같은 인사를 쓸 기회를 꼭 만들어 주세요.

conversations.title: Weather and small talk (polite)
conversations.situation: You're hanging out with your language exchange partner and start chatting about how nice the weather's been.
conversations.tip: Weather is the easiest opener with someone you don't know well yet. Agree (그러니까요/맞아요), add one small opinion, then pivot to a plan — that's how 해요체 small talk turns into actually hanging out.

turns.ko: 와 오늘 날씨 진짜 좋네요 완전 봄이에요
turns.romanization: wa oneul nalssi jinjja jonneyo wanjeon bomieyo
turns.en: Wow the weather today is really nice, totally spring

turns.prompt: Agree and add how you feel about it

choices.ko: 그러니까요ㅋㅋ 이런 날엔 어디 나가고 싶어요
choices.romanization: geureonikkayokk ireon naren eodi nagago sipeoyo
choices.en: Right lol on days like this I just wanna go somewhere
choices.feedback: 그러니까요 agrees, then a small opinion opens the door to a plan. ㅋㅋ keeps 해요체 from sounding stiff.

choices.en: Today's temperature is above the seasonal average.
choices.feedback: This is weather-report language. 해요체 with a partner is friendly, not 합니다체.

choices.en: Yes, nice weather.
choices.feedback: Polite but flat — you agree and add nothing, so the small talk dies right there.

turns.ko: ㅋㅋㅋ 그쵸 요즘 집에만 있기 너무 아까워요
turns.romanization: kkk geuchyo yojeum jibeman itgi neomu akkawoyo
turns.en: Lol right, it feels like such a waste to just stay home these days

turns.prompt: Strongly agree and relate it to yourself

choices.ko: 헐 인정이요ㅋㅋ 저도 주말 내내 집에만 있었어요
choices.romanization: heol injeongiyokk jeodo jumal naenae jibeman isseosseoyo
choices.en: Ugh facts lol I stayed home all weekend too
choices.feedback: 헐 인정 is natural agreement even in 해요체, and sharing your own weekend makes it mutual instead of one-sided.

choices.ko: 외출을 줄이면 건강 관리에 도움이 됩니다.
choices.romanization: oechureul jurimyeon geongang gwallie doumi doemnida.
choices.en: Cutting down on going out helps with health management.
choices.feedback: Reads like a public notice — it neither agrees nor shares anything about you.

choices.en: Do you like staying home?
choices.feedback: Slightly contrary and turns the spotlight on them — it breaks the agreeing flow you just had.

turns.ko: ㅋㅋㅋ 우리 둘 다 집에만 있었네요 진짜
turns.romanization: kkk uri dul da jibeman isseonneyo jinjja
turns.en: Lol we've both been staying home this whole time

turns.prompt: Laugh it off and suggest going out somewhere

choices.ko: ㅋㅋㅋ 맞아요 근데 오늘은 나가요! 한강 갈래요?
choices.romanization: kkk majayo geunde oneureun nagayo! hangang gallaeyo?
choices.en: Lol true, but let's go out today! wanna hit the Han River?
choices.feedback: Agree with a laugh, then pitch something concrete (한강 갈래요?) — that's how small talk becomes a real plan.

choices.en: I strongly recommend outdoor activities.
choices.feedback: Brochure language. You're not advising a stranger, you're inviting someone out.

choices.en: Right, let's go out today.
choices.feedback: The idea is right but it drops into 반말 — you two are on 해요체 terms, so it lands as too familiar too fast.

turns.ko: 오 한강 좋아요!! 가서 치맥 해요 ㅋㅋ
turns.romanization: o hangang joayo!! gaseo chimae kaeyo kk
turns.en: Oh the Han River sounds great!! let's get chicken and beer there lol

turns.prompt: Get hyped and say let's head out now

choices.ko: 오 완전 좋아요ㅋㅋ 날씨도 좋은데 지금 바로 가요!
choices.romanization: o wanjeon joayokk nalssido joeunde jigeum baro gayo!
choices.en: Oh totally down lol the weather's nice so let's go right now!
choices.feedback: 완전 좋아요 + 지금 바로 가요 locks the plan with real energy — 해요체 can be just as excited as 반말.

choices.ko: 치킨과 맥주 섭취 후 귀가 시간을 정하시지요.
choices.romanization: chikingwa maekju seopchwi hu gwiga siganeul jeonghasijiyo.
choices.en: Let us set a return time after consuming chicken and beer.
choices.feedback: Over-formal and weirdly logistical — it sucks the fun out of an easy yes.

choices.en: The weather's really nice today, isn't it?
choices.feedback: Loops back to the opening weather line instead of answering the invitation.

buddyCard.instructionKo: 날씨 좋은 날 같이 있는 언어교환 파트너 역할을 해 주세요. 서로 해요체로 말하는 사이예요. 오늘 날씨가 좋다고 천천히 말하고, 어디에 놀러 갈지 물어봐 주세요.

conversations.title: Inviting a new friend for coffee (polite)
conversations.situation: You met someone at a meetup a while back and text them to grab coffee this weekend.
conversations.tip: With someone you've only met once or twice, a soft 우리 ~할까요? is the perfect invite. React first, then ask one follow-up each turn so the details get settled without either of you feeling pushy.

turns.ko: 안녕하세요! 저번에 보고 진짜 오랜만이에요ㅋㅋ
turns.romanization: annyeonghaseyo! jeobeone bogo jinjja oraenmanieyokk
turns.en: Hi! it's been ages since we met last time lol

turns.prompt: Agree it's been a while and suggest meeting for coffee soon.

choices.en: I know right haha, should we grab coffee sometime soon?
choices.feedback: Matches their energy, and 커피 한잔할까요? is the natural soft invite — low pressure, easy to say yes to.

choices.en: I'd like to treat you to tea after so long.
choices.feedback: 대접하고 싶습니다 is old-fashioned and formal — it sounds like hosting a client, not texting a new friend.

choices.en: Yes, it's been a while.
choices.feedback: Polite but it stops there — no invite, so the thread just fizzles out.

turns.ko: 완전 좋아요! 언제 볼까요?
turns.romanization: wanjeon joayo! eonje bolkkayo?
turns.en: Totally down! when should we meet?

turns.prompt: Propose Saturday afternoon and check if it works for them.

choices.en: How about Saturday afternoon? are you free?
choices.feedback: A concrete time plus 시간 괜찮아요? keeps the decision shared instead of dictating it.

choices.en: Please confirm your schedule.
choices.feedback: 귀하 is business-letter language — nobody texts a friend like this, however new.

choices.en: I like coffee.
choices.feedback: Doesn't answer when to meet — it drifts away from the actual question.

turns.ko: 토요일 좋아요 근데 어디서 볼까요?
turns.romanization: toyoil joayo geunde eodiseo bolkkayo?
turns.en: Saturday works, but where should we meet?

turns.prompt: Suggest a cafe near them and offer to send the location.

choices.ko: 그럼 사시는 동네 근처 카페 어때요? 위치 보낼게요
choices.romanization: geureom sasineun dongne geuncheo kape eottaeyo? wichi bonaelgeyo
choices.en: Then how about a cafe near where you live? I'll send the spot
choices.feedback: Picking a place that's easy for them + 위치 보낼게요 is exactly how you wrap up details in a friendly way.

choices.en: I'll inform you separately once a venue is selected.
choices.feedback: 별도 안내드리겠습니다 sounds like an event organizer's email, not a coffee plan.

choices.en: Shall we meet Saturday afternoon?
choices.feedback: You already settled Saturday — repeating it stalls the plan instead of answering 어디서.

turns.ko: 오키 그럼 토요일에 봐요!
turns.romanization: oki geureom toyoire bwayo!
turns.en: Okay, see you Saturday then!

turns.prompt: Say you're looking forward to it.

choices.en: Nice, really looking forward to it, see you then!
choices.feedback: 기대돼요 adds warmth and 그때 봐요 closes cleanly — friendly 해요체 without going stiff.

choices.en: I shall see you then.
choices.feedback: 뵙겠습니다 is honorific — you'd say it to a boss, not to someone you're getting coffee with.

choices.en: Shall we grab coffee?
choices.feedback: The plan is already set — re-inviting loops the conversation back awkwardly.

buddyCard.instructionKo: 최근에 알게 된 친구 역할을 해 주세요. 서로 해요체로 말하는 사이예요. 이번 주말에 커피를 마실 수 있는지 묻고, 토요일 오후에 어디서 만날지 함께 정해 주세요.

conversations.title: Figuring out lunch with a coworker (polite)
conversations.situation: It's lunchtime and a coworker you're friendly with asks what you two should eat.
conversations.tip: "아무거나 괜찮아요" feels polite but it stalls the decision. With a coworker, give a soft preference plus one real suggestion so they aren't stuck choosing alone.

turns.ko: 벌써 점심시간이네요ㅋㅋ 오늘 뭐 먹을까요?
turns.romanization: beolsseo jeomsimsiganineyokk oneul mwo meogeulkkayo?
turns.en: It's already lunchtime lol what should we eat today?

turns.prompt: Say you're starving and ask if they have anything in mind.

choices.ko: 헐 저 완전 배고파요ㅠㅠ 드시고 싶은 거 있어요?
choices.romanization: heol jeo wanjeon baegopayoyuyu deusigo sipeun geo isseoyo?
choices.en: Ugh I'm starving :( is there anything you feel like?
choices.feedback: Reacts with energy, and 드시고 싶은 거 있어요? invites their idea instead of dead-ending the decision.

choices.en: I am very hungry.
choices.feedback: 고픕니다 is 합니다체 — far too formal for deciding lunch with a coworker you eat with regularly.

choices.en: Anything's fine.
choices.feedback: Sounds easygoing but it dumps the whole decision on them and the conversation goes nowhere.

turns.ko: 음… 어제 치킨 먹어서 좀 느끼해요
turns.romanization: eum… eoje chikin meogeoseo jom neukkihaeyo
turns.en: Hmm… I had chicken yesterday so I'm kinda sick of greasy stuff

turns.prompt: Empathize and suggest something light like kalguksu.

choices.ko: 아 그쵸ㅋㅋ 그럼 칼국수 같은 거 어때요?
choices.romanization: a geuchyokk geureom kalguksu gateun geo eottaeyo?
choices.en: Ah right lol then how about something like kalguksu?
choices.feedback: 그쵸 shows you get it, and a concrete suggestion (칼국수) actually moves the decision forward.

choices.en: Greasy food is harmful to your health.
choices.feedback: Lecture-y and formal — they shared a preference, not a health question.

choices.en: Then let's have chicken again today!
choices.feedback: They just said they're sick of greasy food — this ignores what they told you.

turns.ko: 오 칼국수 좋아요! 근데 거기 항상 줄 길지 않아요?
turns.romanization: o kalguksu joayo! geunde geogi hangsang jul gilji anayo?
turns.en: Oh kalguksu sounds good! but isn't there always a line there?

turns.prompt: Agree it gets busy and suggest going a bit early.

choices.ko: 맞아요 점심엔 웨이팅 길죠ㅋㅋ 좀 일찍 갈까요?
choices.romanization: majayo jeomsimen weiting giljyokk jom iljjik galkkayo?
choices.en: Yeah the wait's long at lunch lol shall we go a bit early?
choices.feedback: 맞아요 confirms their worry, then 좀 일찍 갈까요? solves it together — agreeing plus fixing is the whole move here.

choices.en: That place is always crowded.
choices.feedback: Just restates their point in stiff 합니다체 and offers no way around the line.

choices.en: Then let's go a bit early.
choices.feedback: Good idea, wrong register — 가자 is 반말, and with a coworker you're on 해요체 terms with it lands too familiar.

turns.ko: 콜! 그럼 지금 나갈까요?
turns.romanization: kol! geureom jigeum nagalkkayo?
turns.en: Deal! shall we head out now?

turns.prompt: Agree and say let's go.

choices.en: Sounds good, let's go let's go!
choices.feedback: 가요 is the 해요체 'let's go,' and doubling it adds a friendly little push of energy.

choices.en: Yes, I will depart now.
choices.feedback: 출발하겠습니다 sounds like an announcement to a superior — just say 가요.

choices.ko: 잠깐만요, 저 아직 배 안 고픈데요.
choices.romanization: jamkkanmanyo, jeo ajik bae an gopeundeyo.
choices.en: Hold on, I'm not actually hungry yet.
choices.feedback: Contradicts what you said at the start and stalls the plan right at the finish line.

buddyCard.instructionKo: 함께 점심을 먹는 회사 동료 역할을 해 주세요. 서로 해요체로 말하는 사이예요. 오늘 뭘 먹을지 물어보고, 느끼하지 않은 메뉴와 나가는 시간을 함께 정해 주세요.

conversations.title: Picking a dessert with a new friend (polite)
conversations.situation: You and a friend you recently met are at a cafe staring at the dessert case, trying to decide.
conversations.tip: In person, fillers (음…, 그러게요) and quick agreement tokens (그쵸) buy you time and show you're listening. Pair one with a suggestion so the decision actually moves.

turns.ko: 와 여기 디저트 다 맛있어 보여요… 뭐 먹을까요?
turns.romanization: wa yeogi dijeoteu da masisseo boyeoyo… mwo meogeulkkayo?
turns.en: Wow everything here looks good… what should we get?

turns.prompt: Agree it all looks good and ask what they're craving.

choices.en: Right lol what are you feeling?
choices.feedback: 그러게요 agrees naturally, and 뭐 드시고 싶어요? throws the choice back so you decide together.

choices.en: Everything looks delicious.
choices.feedback: 보입니다 is 합니다체 — too formal facing a cake display with a friend.

choices.en: Does all the dessert here look good?
choices.feedback: Just echoes what they said as a question — it adds nothing and asks them to repeat themselves.

turns.ko: 저는 치즈케이크? 근데 요즘 약과 쿠키도 핫하잖아요
turns.romanization: jeoneun chijeukeikeu? geunde yojeum yakgwa kukido hatajanayo
turns.en: Cheesecake for me? but yakgwa cookies are trendy these days too

turns.prompt: Suggest splitting both so you don't have to choose.

choices.ko: 오 그럼 둘 다 시켜서 나눠 먹을까요?
choices.romanization: o geureom dul da sikyeoseo nanwo meogeulkkayo?
choices.en: Oh then shall we get both and share?
choices.feedback: Solves the indecision, and 나눠 먹을까요? includes them — a classic friendly cafe move.

choices.en: Yakgwa is a traditional Korean sweet.
choices.feedback: A random fact dump that ignores the actual choice the two of you are making.

choices.en: Do as you please.
choices.feedback: Polite on paper but cold — it sounds like you don't want to decide with them.

turns.ko: 오 좋아요! 음료는 뭐 마실래요?
turns.romanization: o joayo! eumnyoneun mwo masillaeyo?
turns.en: Oh nice! what do you want to drink?

turns.prompt: Say iced americano and ask what they're getting.

choices.ko: 저는 아아요! 어떤 거 마실 거예요?
choices.romanization: jeoneun aayo! eotteon geo masil geoyeyo?
choices.en: Iced americano for me! what are you getting?
choices.feedback: 아아 (iced americano) is everyday slang and works fine in 해요체, and the question back keeps it bouncing.

choices.en: I will have an iced americano.
choices.feedback: This is what you say to the barista — with a friend it's just 저는 아아요!

choices.en: Coffee is bad for you.
choices.feedback: Turns a fun choice into a lecture and dodges their question.

turns.ko: 저는 라떼요! 자리 잡고 있어요, 제가 주문할게요
turns.romanization: jeoneul latteyo! jari japgo isseoyo, jega jumunhalgeyo
turns.en: Latte for me! grab us a seat, I'll order

turns.prompt: Offer to pay this round instead.

choices.en: Okay! but this round's on me lol
choices.feedback: 제가 살게요 is warm and natural, and offering back keeps the give-and-take going with someone new.

choices.en: I shall take care of the payment.
choices.feedback: 하도록 하겠습니다 reads like staff at a counter — friends say 제가 살게요.

choices.en: Yes, come back quickly.
choices.feedback: A bit bossy and flat when they just offered to go order for you.

buddyCard.instructionKo: 카페에서 같이 디저트를 고르는, 새로 알게 된 친구 역할을 해 주세요. 서로 해요체로 말하는 사이예요. 뭘 먹고 싶은지와 어떤 음료를 마실지 물어보고, 둘이 나눠 먹자고 제안해 주세요.
buddyCard.reactionKo: 좋아요, 그럼 둘 다 시켜서 나눠 먹어요!

conversations.title: Which top looks better (polite)
conversations.situation: You're out shopping with an acquaintance and they hold up two tops and ask you to pick one.
conversations.tip: When someone asks you to choose between two things, don't hedge with 둘 다 좋아요 — react (오/음), pick a side, and give a quick reason. A clear opinion with a why is what they actually want, even in 해요체.

turns.ko: 이거 둘 중에 뭐가 나아요?? 한번 봐 주세요ㅋㅋ
turns.romanization: igeo dul junge mwoga naayo?? hanbeon bwa juseyokk
turns.en: Which of these two is better?? take a look lol

turns.prompt: React and ask what the occasion is before choosing.

choices.ko: 오 둘 다 예쁜데요ㅋㅋ 어디 입고 가실 거예요?
choices.romanization: o dul da yeppeundeyokk eodi ipgo gasil geoyeyo?
choices.en: Oh they're both cute lol where are you gonna wear it?
choices.feedback: 오 reacts, and 어디 입고 가실 거예요? gets the context you need to actually help — it keeps the chat rolling too.

choices.en: Both suit you well.
choices.feedback: 어울리십니다 is 합니다체 — way too formal standing next to them in a shop. Try 둘 다 예쁜데요.

choices.en: Buying clothes again? your closet's gonna explode.
choices.feedback: Teasing like this only works with a close friend — with an acquaintance it just reads as nagging.

turns.ko: 주말에 소개팅이요ㅋㅋㅋ 첫인상 중요하잖아요
turns.romanization: jumare sogaetingiyokkk cheosinsang jungyohajanayo
turns.en: A blind date this weekend lol first impressions matter you know

turns.prompt: Pick the white one and give a quick reason.

choices.ko: 헐 소개팅이요?? 그럼 무조건 흰색이요! 깔끔해 보여요
choices.romanization: heol sogaetingiyo?? geureom mujogeon huinsaegiyo! kkalkkeumhae boyeoyo
choices.en: Whoa a blind date?? then definitely the white one! it looks clean
choices.feedback: Reacts to the news, then commits to a pick with a reason (깔끔해 보여요) — exactly the help they asked for.

choices.en: The white top looks more tidy.
choices.feedback: Textbook-stiff. The opinion is fine but 합니다체 makes it sound like a product review.

choices.en: I can't tell which one's better.
choices.feedback: Dodges the question — they asked you to choose, so pick one and say why.

turns.ko: 오 그쵸? 근데 흰색은 음식 흘리면 티 나잖아요ㅠ
turns.romanization: o geuchyo? geunde huinsaegeun eumsi keullimyeon ti najanayoyu
turns.en: Oh right? but white shows stains if I spill food ㅠ

turns.prompt: Agree with the worry but hold your pick.

choices.ko: ㅋㅋㅋ 그건 그래요 근데 조심하면 되죠! 흰색이 훨 나아요
choices.romanization: kkk geugeon geuraeyo geunde josimhamyeon doejyo! huinsaegi hwol naayo
choices.en: Lol true, but just be careful! white's way better
choices.feedback: 그건 그래요 validates the worry, then you hold your pick — that back-and-forth is what lands the decision.

choices.ko: 흰 옷은 오염에 취약하므로 주의가 필요합니다.
choices.romanization: huin oseun oyeome chwiyakameuro juuiga piryohamnida.
choices.en: White clothes are prone to stains so caution is required.
choices.feedback: Sounds like a care label, not someone helping them feel good about a choice.

choices.en: Then just buy the black one.
choices.feedback: Flip-flops the moment they hesitate — wishy-washy when they wanted you to be sure.

turns.ko: ㅇㅋㅋㅋ 결정했어요 흰색 살게요! 고마워요
turns.romanization: ngkkk gyeoljeonghaesseoyo huinsaek salgeyo! gomawoyo
turns.en: Okok lol decided, I'll get the white one! thanks

turns.prompt: Hype them up and ask to see it on later.

choices.ko: ㅋㅋ 잘 고르셨어요! 나중에 입은 사진 보내 주세요
choices.romanization: kk jal goreusyeosseoyo! najunge ibeun sajin bonae juseyo
choices.en: Lol good pick! send me a photo of you in it later
choices.feedback: 잘 고르셨어요 closes it warmly and asking for a photo keeps the thread alive for next time.

choices.en: An excellent choice. Please send a photo.
choices.feedback: Reads like a shop clerk closing a sale — the 십니다 puts distance where you wanted warmth.

choices.ko: 소개팅 잘 안 되면 옷 탓이에요ㅋㅋ
choices.romanization: sogaeting jal an doemyeon ot tasieyokk
choices.en: If the date flops it's the outfit's fault lol
choices.feedback: The joke lands flat and adds pressure right when they finally felt good about the choice.

buddyCard.instructionKo: 같이 쇼핑을 온 지인 역할을 해 주세요. 서로 해요체로 말하는 사이예요. 상의 두 벌 중에 뭐가 더 나은지 묻고, 왜 그걸 골랐는지도 물어봐 주세요.

conversations.title: Help a coworker pick a gift
conversations.situation: A coworker messages you for help choosing a birthday gift for someone on your team.
conversations.tip: With a coworker you're friendly with, keep 해요체 but stay warm. Ask about budget and taste first (예산 얼마 정도 생각해요? / 뭐에 빠져 있어요?) — narrowing it down is what makes the help useful.

turns.ko: 다음 주가 지민 씨 생일인데 뭐 선물하죠? 좀 도와주세요ㅠ
turns.romanization: daeum juga jimin ssi saengirinde mwo seonmulhajyo? jom dowajuseyoyu
turns.en: It's Jimin's birthday next week — what should I get? Help me out ㅠ

turns.prompt: Ask how much they're thinking of spending.

choices.ko: 오 벌써 생일이네요ㅋㅋ 예산 얼마 정도 생각해요?
choices.romanization: o beolsseo saengirineyokk yesan eolma jeongdo saenggakaeyo?
choices.en: Oh it's their birthday already lol — how much are you thinking of spending?
choices.feedback: Reacts first (오 벌써), then 예산 얼마 정도 생각해요? narrows it down. Friendly 해요체 with ㅋㅋ keeps it from sounding like an interview.

choices.en: What budget have you allocated? (formal)
choices.feedback: 책정하셨습니까 is 합니다체 budget-meeting language. Same question, but 예산 얼마 정도 생각해요? is what a coworker actually says.

choices.en: It's the thought that counts with gifts.
choices.feedback: Polite and grammatical, but it's a platitude — they asked for real ideas, so this gives them nothing to work with.

turns.ko: 한 5만 원 안쪽요? 너무 부담 주긴 싫어서요ㅋㅋ
turns.romanization: han 5man won anjjogyo? neomu budam jugin sireoseoyokk
turns.en: Under 50k or so? I don't want to make it too much lol

turns.prompt: React to the budget, then ask what they're into before suggesting.

choices.ko: 오케이 적당하네요ㅋㅋ 근데 그분 요즘 뭐에 빠져 있어요?
choices.romanization: okei jeokdanghaneyokk geunde geubun yojeum mwoe ppajyeo isseoyo?
choices.en: Okay, that's reasonable lol — but what are they into these days?
choices.feedback: Confirms the budget, then asks about taste. Gathering one more fact before recommending is what makes you sound genuinely helpful, not just polite.

choices.en: That amount is deemed appropriate. (formal)
choices.feedback: 사료됩니다 is written-report language. Even at work, spoken 해요체 would just be 적당하네요.

choices.en: Is there anything you can even buy for 50k?
choices.feedback: Grammatical, but it dismisses the budget they just set instead of working inside it — it makes them defend themselves rather than keep planning.

turns.ko: 요즘 향수에 진심이더라고요ㅋㅋ 인스타에 맨날 올려요
turns.romanization: yojeum hyangsue jinsimideoragoyokk inseutae maennal ollyeoyo
turns.en: They're really into perfume lately lol — they post it on Instagram all the time

turns.prompt: Light up and suggest a diffuser or a mini perfume.

choices.ko: 오 그럼 답 나왔네요ㅋㅋ 디퓨저나 미니 향수 어때요?
choices.romanization: o geureom dam nawanneyokk dipyujeona mini hyangsu eottaeyo?
choices.en: Oh then we've got our answer lol — how about a diffuser or a mini perfume?
choices.feedback: 답 나왔네요 shows you picked up their hint, and two concrete options let them choose. Reaction plus suggestion is the pattern that moves a decision.

choices.ko: 향수 또는 디퓨저를 선물하시는 것을 추천드립니다.
choices.romanization: hyangsu ttoneun dipyujeoreul seonmulhasineun geoseul chucheondeurimnida.
choices.en: I recommend gifting a perfume or a diffuser. (formal)
choices.feedback: 추천드립니다 reads like a shopping site. Between coworkers it's 디퓨저나 향수 어때요?

choices.en: Perfume is hard to pick since it's a taste thing.
choices.feedback: Polite 해요체 but it shuts down the lead they just handed you. If you raise a problem, pair it with an alternative.

turns.ko: 오 디퓨저 좋네요! 근데 어디서 사죠? 추천 좀요ㅋㅋ
turns.romanization: o dipyujeo jonneyo! geunde eodiseo sajyo? chucheon jomyokk
turns.en: Oh a diffuser sounds good! But where do I buy one? Give me a rec lol

turns.prompt: Offer to send a link to a shop you like.

choices.ko: 제가 자주 가는 데 있어요ㅋㅋ 링크 보내 드릴게요!
choices.romanization: jega jaju ganeun de isseoyokk ringkeu bonae deurilgeyo!
choices.en: There's a place I go to a lot lol — I'll send you the link!
choices.feedback: 보내 드릴게요 offers a concrete next step. Ending on an action you'll take is a warm way to close a favor between coworkers.

choices.ko: 제가 즐겨 이용하는 매장 링크를 전송해 드리겠습니다.
choices.romanization: jega jeulgyeo iyonghaneun maejang ningkeureul jeonsonghae deurigetseumnida.
choices.en: I shall transmit a link to the store I frequent. (formal)
choices.feedback: 전송해 드리겠습니다 is 합니다체 and sounds automated. 링크 보내 드릴게요 says the same thing like a person.

choices.en: It all comes up if you just search online.
choices.feedback: Perfectly polite, but they asked you specifically — pointing them back to a search engine reads as brushing them off.

buddyCard.instructionKo: 같은 팀 동료의 생일 선물을 함께 고르는 회사 동료 역할을 해 주세요. 서로 해요체로 말하면서, 무엇을 사면 좋을지와 어디서 살지 물어봐 주세요. 학습자는 초급이니 천천히 말해 주세요.

conversations.title: Recommending a drama to a language partner
conversations.situation: Your language exchange partner messages you asking for a drama to binge this weekend.
conversations.tip: 해요체 doesn't have to be stiff. React first (오!), then sell the pick with a quick reason (완전 꿀잼이라 순삭이에요) — slang works fine in 해요체 and keeps you from sounding like a textbook.

turns.ko: 주말에 정주행할 드라마 없을까요? 추천 좀 해 주세요ㅠ
turns.romanization: jumare jeongjuhaenghal deurama eopseulkkayo? chucheon jom hae juseyoyu
turns.en: Is there a drama I could binge this weekend? Recommend me something ㅠ

turns.prompt: Ask what genre they're in the mood for.

choices.en: What are you in the mood for these days? Romance? Thriller?
choices.feedback: 뭐 땡겨요? is casual slang that still lands as 해요체, and offering two genres makes it easy for them to answer.

choices.en: Which genre do you prefer? (formal)
choices.feedback: 선호하십니까 is 합니다체 survey language. With a language partner, 뭐 땡겨요? gets the same info without the distance.

choices.en: I don't really watch dramas.
choices.feedback: Fine 해요체, but they asked you for a rec — leading with what you don't do ends the thread instead of helping.

turns.ko: 스릴러요! 몰입되는 거 보고 싶어요
turns.romanization: seurilleoyo! moripdoeneun geo bogo sipeoyo
turns.en: Thriller! I want something gripping

turns.prompt: React and recommend one, selling how fun it is.

choices.ko: 오, 그럼 제가 추천작 링크 하나 보낼게요. 완전 꿀잼이라 순삭이에요
choices.romanization: o, geureom jega chucheonjang ningkeu hana bonaelgeyo. wanjeon kkuljaemira sunsagieyo
choices.en: Oh, then I'll send you a link to one I recommend. It's so good you'll fly through it.
choices.feedback: Delivers an actual pick and sells it. 꿀잼/순삭 are register-neutral slang, so they sit comfortably inside 해요체.

choices.en: That work is very thrilling. (formal)
choices.feedback: 흥미진진합니다 reads like a review blurb. 완전 꿀잼이에요 is the same praise in a voice a real person uses.

choices.en: Hmm, nothing really comes to mind.
choices.feedback: Natural 해요체, but it doesn't deliver what they asked for and leaves them with nothing to reply to.

turns.ko: 오 몇 부작이에요? 너무 길면 부담돼요
turns.romanization: o myeot bujagieyo? neomu gilmyeon budamdwaeyo
turns.en: Oh how many episodes? If it's too long that's a lot

turns.prompt: Say it's short, and nudge them to start tonight.

choices.en: It's 8 episodes, so you can finish in a day lol — start it tonight
choices.feedback: Answers the question, then 오늘 바로 보세요 gives a friendly push. In 해요체, -세요 works as an easy nudge, not an order.

choices.en: It is 8 episodes in total and viewing is recommended. (formal)
choices.feedback: 권장드립니다 is customer-service 합니다체. Same content, but it makes a fun rec sound like a notice.

choices.en: You're curious how many episodes?
choices.feedback: Grammatical, but it just mirrors their question back instead of answering — the conversation stalls.

turns.ko: 오케이 그럼 오늘 1화 볼게요
turns.romanization: okei geureom oneul 1hwa bolgeyo
turns.en: Okay, then I'll start episode 1 today

turns.prompt: Tease what's coming and ask them to report back.

choices.ko: ㅋㅋ 보고 후기 톡해 주세요! 4화부터 미쳤어요
choices.romanization: kk bogo hugi tokae juseyo! 4hwabuteo michyeosseoyo
choices.en: lol message me your thoughts after! It goes crazy from ep 4
choices.feedback: A teaser plus 후기 톡해 주세요 invites them back — a sign-off that opens the next conversation instead of ending this one.

choices.ko: 시청 후 감상을 공유해 주시기 바랍니다.
choices.romanization: sicheong hu gamsangeul gongyuhae jusigi baramnida.
choices.en: Please share your impressions after viewing. (formal)
choices.feedback: 주시기 바랍니다 is announcement language. 후기 톡해 주세요 is the same request, warm instead of official.

choices.en: Okay, bye.
choices.feedback: Polite and correct, but nobody's leaving — a goodbye here cuts off a chat that was still going.

buddyCard.instructionKo: 주말에 몰아서 볼 드라마를 찾는 언어교환 파트너 역할을 해 주세요. 서로 해요체로 말하면서 추천을 부탁하고, 추천을 들으면 몇 부작인지 물어봐 주세요. 학습자는 초급이니 천천히 말해 주세요.

conversations.title: Deciding what to watch with a new friend
conversations.situation: You're hanging out with someone you recently got to know and you can't decide what to put on Netflix.
conversations.tip: With someone you've just gotten to know, 해요체 is the comfortable middle. Don't say 아무거나 — offer two options or a concrete pick, and react to theirs so you actually land on something.

turns.ko: 넷플 뭐 볼까요? 볼 게 없네요
turns.romanization: netpeul mwo bolkkayo? bol ge eopsneyo
turns.en: What should we put on Netflix? There's nothing to watch

turns.prompt: Agree, then offer two options.

choices.en: Right lol — movie, or maybe a variety show?
choices.feedback: 그러게요 is the 해요체 agreement token, and two options give them something easy to pick from instead of an open question.

choices.en: What do you wish to view? (formal)
choices.feedback: 원하십니까 is hotel-staff 합니다체 — far too distant for two people on a couch. 뭐 볼까요? covers it.

choices.en: Netflix has a lot of content.
choices.feedback: Perfectly grammatical 해요체 that states the obvious. It doesn't help you two narrow anything down.

turns.ko: 음, 머리 비우고 볼 수 있는 가벼운 예능요?
turns.romanization: eum, meori biugo bol su inneun gabyeoun yeneungyo?
turns.en: Hmm, maybe a light variety show I can watch without thinking?

turns.prompt: Like the idea and suggest the show everyone's talking about.

choices.ko: 오 좋아요, 요즘 다들 보는 그거 볼래요?
choices.romanization: o joayo, yojeum dadeul boneun geugeo bollaeyo?
choices.en: Oh nice — wanna watch the one everyone's on about lately?
choices.feedback: 오 좋아요 accepts their direction, then a concrete suggestion closes in on a pick. 볼래요? invites without pushing.

choices.en: I propose the viewing of a variety program. (formal)
choices.feedback: 제안드립니다 belongs in a meeting. 그거 볼래요? is the same proposal at the right distance.

choices.en: Documentaries are more worthwhile than variety shows.
choices.feedback: Grammatical, but it overrides what they just said they wanted and comes off preachy.

turns.ko: 아 그거 1화만 봤는데 개웃기더라고요ㅋㅋ
turns.romanization: a geugeo 1hwaman bwanneunde gaeutgideoragoyokk
turns.en: Ah I only saw episode 1 of that, it was hilarious lol

turns.prompt: Match their reaction and suggest starting from episode 2.

choices.en: Right lol — then let's put on episode 2
choices.feedback: 그쵸 matches their energy in 해요체, and 틀어요 turns the chat into an action. Agreement plus a move is what ends indecision.

choices.en: Then I shall proceed to play from episode 2. (formal)
choices.feedback: 하도록 하겠습니다 is 합니다체 — jarringly official for pressing play on a couch. Just 2화부터 틀어요.

choices.en: Was episode 1 really that funny?
choices.feedback: Natural 해요체, but it just re-asks what they told you rather than moving to actually watching.

turns.ko: 콜이요 근데 저 팝콘 먹고 싶어요ㅋㅋ
turns.romanization: koriyo geunde jeo papkon meokgo sipeoyokk
turns.en: Deal, but I kind of want popcorn lol

turns.prompt: Agree and offer to grab snacks.

choices.ko: ㅋㅋ 좋아요, 제가 간식 챙겨 올게요. 잠깐만요!
choices.romanization: kk joayo, jega gansik chaenggyeo olgeyo. jamkkanmanyo!
choices.en: Lol okay, I'll grab snacks. Hold on!
choices.feedback: 챙겨 올게요 volunteers you for the small task, and 잠깐만요 is the everyday 해요체 'hold on' — easy and warm.

choices.en: I shall prepare and bring snacks. (formal)
choices.feedback: 준비해 오도록 하겠습니다 sounds like catering staff. 간식 챙겨 올게요 is the same offer, human-sized.

choices.en: Popcorn is something you eat at the theater.
choices.feedback: Grammatical 해요체, but contradicting a harmless craving just derails the cozy plan you two built.

buddyCard.instructionKo: 같이 영상을 보려고 하는, 새로 알게 된 친구 역할을 해 주세요. 서로 해요체로 말하면서 무엇을 볼지 묻고, 가볍게 볼 예능을 보고 싶다고 말해 주세요. 학습자는 초급이니 천천히 말해 주세요.

conversations.title: Hearing about a new hobby
conversations.situation: Someone from your club mentions they just picked up baking, and you're curious to hear about it.
conversations.tip: Curiosity carries the conversation. Stack follow-ups (진짜요? / 얼마나 됐어요? / 뭐 만들었어요?) and react warmly — in 해요체 the reactions do the friendliness work.

turns.ko: 저 요즘 베이킹 시작했거든요
turns.romanization: jeo yojeum beiking sijakaetgeodeunyo
turns.en: So I started baking recently

turns.prompt: React with surprise and ask why baking.

choices.en: Whoa, really? Why baking all of a sudden?
choices.feedback: 헐 진짜요? reacts before asking — 헐 is register-neutral, so it warms up 해요체 without turning it into 반말. Then 왜요? opens them up.

choices.en: I am surprised to hear you started baking. (formal)
choices.feedback: 놀랍습니다 states surprise instead of showing it. 합니다체 makes a genuine reaction sound like a written comment.

choices.ko: 아 그렇군요. 저도 밥 먹어야 되는데요.
choices.romanization: a geureokunyo. jeodo bam meogeoya doeneundeyo.
choices.en: Ah, I see. I should eat something too.
choices.feedback: Polite and grammatical, but it drops what they shared and swerves to yourself — their excitement has nowhere to go.

turns.ko: 그냥 스트레스 풀려고요? 빵 만들면 좀 힐링되더라고요
turns.romanization: geunyang seuteureseu pullyeogoyo? ppang mandeulmyeon jom hillingdoedeoragoyo
turns.en: Just to de-stress, I guess? Making bread is kind of therapeutic

turns.prompt: Show you get it and ask how long they've been doing it.

choices.ko: 오, 그럴 것 같아요. 근데 시작한 지 얼마나 됐어요?
choices.romanization: o, geureol geot gatayo. geunde sijakan ji eolmana dwaesseoyo?
choices.en: Oh, I can see that. How long have you been doing it?
choices.feedback: 그럴 것 같아요 validates their reason, and the follow-up keeps the spotlight on them. Validate-then-ask is the engine of this whole chat.

choices.ko: 베이킹의 치유 효과에 대해 동의하는 바입니다.
choices.romanization: beikingui chiyu hyogwae daehae donguihaneun baimnida.
choices.en: I concur regarding the therapeutic effects of baking. (formal)
choices.feedback: 동의하는 바입니다 is speech-giving language. Face to face, 그럴 것 같아요 is all the agreement you need.

choices.en: So when are you going to give me some bread?
choices.feedback: Grammatical 해요체, but jumping to what you get out of it this early pulls focus off their story.

turns.ko: 한두 달요? 처음엔 진짜 다 망했는데 요즘 좀 늘었어요
turns.romanization: handu daryo? cheoeumen jinjja da manghaenneunde yojeum jom neureosseoyo
turns.en: Like two months? At first everything flopped, but I've gotten better lately

turns.prompt: Cheer them on and ask what they made recently.

choices.en: That's awesome, I'm jealous lol — what did you make recently?
choices.feedback: 대박 and ㅋㅋ carry the warmth while 부러워요 keeps the 해요체 clean, and the question invites the next story.

choices.en: I presume it is the result of continuous effort. (formal)
choices.feedback: 사료됩니다 is report-writing 합니다체 — praise this stiff reads as sarcasm in a friendly chat.

choices.en: Two months means you're still a beginner, I guess.
choices.feedback: Correct 해요체, but it deflates the progress they were proud of instead of celebrating it.

turns.ko: 지난주에 휘낭시에 구웠는데 그건 좀 성공했어요ㅋㅋ
turns.romanization: jinanjue hwinangsie guwonneunde geugeon jom seonggonghaesseoyokk
turns.en: I baked financiers last week and those actually turned out lol

turns.prompt: Hint playfully that you'd like to try one.

choices.ko: 오, 휘낭시에ㅋㅋ 다음에 저도 하나 맛봐도 돼요?
choices.romanization: o, hwinangsiekk daeume jeodo hana matbwado dwaeyo?
choices.en: Oh, financiers lol — can I try one next time?
choices.feedback: 맛봐도 돼요? asks permission lightly, and 다음에 leaves the door open for a next meetup — a great way to close with someone you're still getting to know.

choices.ko: 다음 기회에 시식할 수 있도록 부탁드립니다.
choices.romanization: daeum gihoee sisikal su itdorok butakdeurimnida.
choices.en: I request the opportunity to taste them at the next occasion. (formal)
choices.feedback: 시식/부탁드립니다 is event-organizer language and clashes with the easy ㅋㅋ tone they set.

choices.en: What's a financier? I'm not interested.
choices.feedback: Grammatical, but announcing you're not interested right after they opened up shuts the whole thing down.

buddyCard.instructionKo: 최근 베이킹을 시작한, 동호회에서 만난 사람 역할을 해 주세요. 서로 해요체로 말하면서 스트레스를 풀려고 시작했다고 말하고, 얼마나 했는지와 최근 무엇을 만들었는지 이야기해 주세요. 학습자는 초급이니 천천히 말해 주세요.
buddyCard.reactionKo: 다음에는 제가 만든 것도 하나 드릴게요!

conversations.title: Climbing plan with a club member
conversations.situation: Someone from your club messages to invite you to an indoor climbing gym this weekend.
conversations.tip: When someone you're still getting to know proposes an activity, react (오 좋아요/콜이요) then ask one practical question (which day, what to bring). That's what turns an invite into a real plan.

turns.ko: 주말에 클라이밍 갈래요?
turns.romanization: jumare keullaiming gallaeyo?
turns.en: Wanna go climbing this weekend?

turns.prompt: React with interest and ask which day.

choices.en: Oh nice — Saturday or Sunday?
choices.feedback: 오 좋아요 says yes with feeling, and asking which day immediately starts building the actual plan.

choices.en: I agree to going climbing this weekend. (formal)
choices.feedback: 동의합니다 sounds like approving a motion. An invite gets 좋아요, not agreement in 합니다체.

choices.en: Is the weather supposed to be nice this weekend?
choices.feedback: Fine 해요체, but it's indoor climbing and you never answered — the invite is left hanging.

turns.ko: 토요일 오전 어때요? 사람 적을 때 가요
turns.romanization: toyoil ojeon eottaeyo? saram jeogeul ttae gayo
turns.en: How about Saturday morning? Let's go when it's less crowded

turns.prompt: Agree, but be honest that you're a beginner.

choices.ko: 콜이요 근데 저 완전 초보인데 괜찮아요?
choices.romanization: koriyo geunde jeo wanjeon choboinde gwaenchanayo?
choices.en: Deal — but I'm a total beginner, is that okay?
choices.feedback: 콜이요 accepts, then a quick honest check gives them something to respond to. Admitting a gap invites help rather than ending the thread.

choices.ko: 저는 클라이밍 경험이 전혀 없는 초보자입니다.
choices.romanization: jeoneun keullaiming gyeongheomi jeonhyeo eopsneun chobojaimnida.
choices.en: I am a beginner with no climbing experience whatsoever. (formal)
choices.feedback: The content is right but 초보자입니다 is a self-introduction at a podium. 저 완전 초보인데 괜찮아요? asks and confesses at once.

choices.ko: 토요일 오전 어때요, 사람 적을 때요?
choices.romanization: toyoil ojeon eottaeyo, saram jeogeul ttaeyo?
choices.en: Saturday morning, when it's less crowded?
choices.feedback: Grammatical, but it repeats their suggestion back word for word — that reads as not having replied at all.

turns.ko: 괜찮아요 제가 다 알려 드릴게요 신발만 빌리면 돼요
turns.romanization: gwaenchanayo jega da allyeo deurilgeyo sinbalman billimyeon dwaeyo
turns.en: It's fine, I'll show you everything — you just need to rent shoes

turns.prompt: Show relief and ask what to bring.

choices.ko: 오 다행이에요ㅋㅋ 그럼 뭐 챙겨 가면 돼요?
choices.romanization: o dahaengieyokk geureom mwo chaenggyeo gamyeon dwaeyo?
choices.en: Oh what a relief lol — so what should I bring?
choices.feedback: 다행이에요 reacts to their reassurance, and 뭐 챙겨 가면 돼요? is the practical question that keeps the plan concrete.

choices.en: I would appreciate it if you could advise me regarding the required items. (formal)
choices.feedback: 안내해 주시면 감사하겠습니다 is email-to-a-stranger politeness — much heavier than the text they just sent you.

choices.ko: 저 클라이밍 말고 등산이 더 좋은데요.
choices.romanization: jeo keullaiming malgo deungsani deo joeundeyo.
choices.en: I'd actually rather go hiking than climbing.
choices.feedback: Natural 해요체, but you already agreed to climbing — changing the plan after they offered to teach you is confusing.

turns.ko: 편한 운동복이랑 물만 챙겨 오세요 끝나고 밥 먹어요
turns.romanization: pyeonhan undongbogirang mulman chaenggyeo oseyo kkeunnago bam meogeoyo
turns.en: Just bring comfy workout clothes and water — let's eat after

turns.prompt: Lock the plan in with some energy.

choices.en: Deal — I'm so excited, see you Saturday!
choices.feedback: 기대돼요 adds real enthusiasm and 토요일에 봐요 confirms the plan. Closing with the day locked in is what makes it feel settled.

choices.en: I shall proceed accordingly. (formal)
choices.feedback: 진행하도록 하겠습니다 is a work confirmation. It's polite, but it reads as zero excitement about the weekend.

choices.en: So who's paying for the food?
choices.feedback: Grammatical, but it gets transactional right at the close. 끝나고 같이 먹어요 first — sort out the bill on the day.

buddyCard.instructionKo: 주말에 함께 클라이밍하고 싶은, 동호회에서 만난 사람 역할을 해 주세요. 서로 해요체로 말하면서 토요일 오전이 괜찮은지와 무엇을 챙겨 올지 물어보고, 처음이어도 도와주겠다고 말해 주세요. 학습자는 초급이니 천천히 말해 주세요.
buddyCard.reactionKo: 걱정 마세요, 제가 옆에서 알려 드릴게요!

conversations.title: Busan or Jeju? (polite)
conversations.situation: Your language exchange partner is texting you to decide whether your weekend trip should be to Busan or Jeju.
conversations.tip: 해요체 is not the same as being distant. Share a real preference with a reason, then bounce it back (어때요? / 그쪽은요?) — friendly 해요체 keeps the decision two-way instead of turning it into a survey.

turns.ko: 그런데 우리 부산 갈까요, 제주 갈까요?
turns.romanization: geureonde uri busan galkkayo, jeju galkkayo?
turns.en: So should we go to Busan or Jeju?

turns.prompt: Give your lean and ask theirs

choices.ko: 음 저는 바다가 보고 싶어서 제주가 끌리는데, 어때요?
choices.romanization: eum jeoneun badaga bogo sipeoseo jejuga kkeullineunde, eottaeyo?
choices.en: Hmm I'm leaning Jeju because I want to see the ocean — how about you?
choices.feedback: A preference plus a reason, then 어때요? hands the turn back — that's what makes 해요체 feel warm instead of formal.

choices.en: May I ask which place you prefer?
choices.feedback: Grammatical, but 여쭤봐도 될까요 is customer-service polite — it interviews your partner instead of chatting with them.

choices.en: Should we go to Busan or Jeju?
choices.feedback: Echoes their question word for word. Polite, but it adds no opinion, so the decision stalls.

turns.ko: 오 제주 좋아요! 근데 비행기값 비싸지 않아요?
turns.romanization: o jeju joayo! geunde bihaenggigaps bissaji anayo?
turns.en: Oh Jeju sounds good! But isn't the flight pricey?

turns.prompt: Acknowledge the concern, stay flexible

choices.ko: 그것도 그렇네요ㅋㅋ 그럼 부산도 괜찮아요. 저는 둘 다 좋아요
choices.romanization: geugeotdo geureonneyokk geureom busando gwaenchanayo. jeoneun dul da joayo
choices.en: That's true tooㅋㅋ Busan works for me then. I like both.
choices.feedback: 그것도 그렇네요 accepts their point out loud, and 저는 둘 다 좋아요 keeps you deciding together. ㅋㅋ softens 해요체 nicely.

choices.en: I will not get involved regarding the flight cost.
choices.feedback: 합니다체 plus 관여하지 않겠습니다 sounds like dodging responsibility at work — far too cold for planning a trip.

choices.en: Is it your first time on a plane?
choices.feedback: Perfectly polite, but it ignores the actual issue (money) and drifts off topic.

turns.ko: 흠 사실 저는 부산 가서 회 먹고 싶긴 해요
turns.romanization: heum sasil jeoneun busan gaseo hoe meokgo sipgin haeyo
turns.en: Hmm honestly I kind of want to go to Busan and eat sashimi.

turns.prompt: Get excited about the food angle

choices.ko: 오 회 좋죠!! 그럼 부산으로 가요, 먹킷리스트 짜요ㅋㅋ
choices.romanization: o hoe jochyo!! geureom busaneuro gayo, meokkinniseuteu jjayokk
choices.en: Oh sashimi, yes!! Let's do Busan then, let's make a food bucket listㅋㅋ
choices.feedback: 좋죠 is an enthusiastic 해요체 agreement, and running with their idea toward a next step (먹킷리스트 짜요) keeps the energy up.

choices.en: Sashimi is a healthy food.
choices.feedback: A textbook fact in 합니다체. It answers nothing and drops the friendly tone in one line.

choices.ko: 왜 갑자기 회 얘기를 하는 거예요?
choices.romanization: wae gapjagi hoe yaegireul haneun geoyeyo?
choices.en: Why are you suddenly talking about sashimi?
choices.feedback: Polite but sounds irritated at a normal suggestion — your partner will stop offering ideas.

turns.ko: 콜콜 부산 가요!! 광안리에서 회에 소주 어때요?
turns.romanization: kolkol busan gayo!! gwangallieseo hoee soju eottaeyo?
turns.en: Deal deal, let's do Busan!! Sashimi and soju at Gwangalli, how about it?

turns.prompt: Lock it in and hype the plan
