choices.ko: 캬 그거죠ㅋㅋ 벌써 설레요 빨리 가요
choices.romanization: kya geugeojyokk beolsseo seolleyo ppalli gayo
choices.en: Ahh that's the oneㅋㅋ I'm already excited, let's go soon.
choices.feedback: 캬 is style-neutral, so it works fine in 해요체, and 벌써 설레요 shares the excitement instead of just agreeing.

choices.en: I will positively consider visiting Gwangalli.
choices.feedback: Office-memo language. It technically says yes but reads like you're stalling a proposal.

choices.en: Is there nothing besides soju?
choices.feedback: Nitpicks the fun suggestion they just made — it deflates the moment right at the close.

buddyCard.instructionKo: 함께 여행을 계획하는 언어교환 파트너 역할을 해 주세요. 부산과 제주 중 어디가 좋은지 해요체로 묻고, 비용이나 먹고 싶은 음식도 물어봐 주세요. 학습자는 초급이니 짧고 천천히 말해 주세요.

conversations.title: Let's study together (polite)
conversations.situation: Someone from your Korean class texts that the exam is close and they have not started, so you suggest studying together.
conversations.tip: 해요체 proposals still sound casual: ~할래요?, ~해요, 어때요?. Suggest, then nail down the details (어디서? 몇 시?) — that's how a classmate turns into a study buddy.

turns.ko: 아 시험 코앞인데 하나도 못 했어요
turns.romanization: a siheom koapinde hanado mo taesseoyo
turns.en: Ugh the exam's right around the corner and I haven't done a thing

turns.prompt: Say you're the same and suggest studying together.

choices.en: Same hereㅋㅋ want to study together?
choices.feedback: 저도요 relates first, then ~할래요? invites. This is the everyday 해요체 way to propose something without sounding pushy.

choices.en: How would it be to study together?
choices.feedback: Correct Korean, but 어떻겠습니까 is meeting-room 합니다체 — nobody invites a classmate like this.

choices.en: It's better to study for exams alone.
choices.feedback: Polite and fine grammatically, but it shuts down the chance to make a plan together.

turns.ko: 오 좋아요! 어디서 할까요?
turns.romanization: o joayo! eodiseo halkkayo?
turns.en: Oh nice! Where should we do it?

turns.prompt: Suggest a cafe and ask if it works.

choices.ko: 학교 앞 카페 어때요? 거기 조용하잖아요
choices.romanization: hakgyo ap kape eottaeyo? geogi joyonghajanayo
choices.en: How about the cafe by school? It's quiet there
choices.feedback: A concrete spot plus a reason (조용하잖아요). ~잖아요 assumes shared knowledge, which is exactly how classmates talk.

choices.en: You decide the place.
choices.feedback: 당신 and 정하세요 land cold and distant — and it dumps the whole decision on them.

choices.en: The library has no seats.
choices.feedback: Only says where NOT to go. They asked for a place, so give one.

turns.ko: 콜! 몇 시에 만날까요?
turns.romanization: kol! myeot sie mannalkkayo?
turns.en: Deal! What time should we meet?

turns.prompt: Propose 2 PM and check it's okay.

choices.ko: 두 시 어때요? 점심 먹고 가요
choices.romanization: du si eottaeyo? jeomsim meokgo gayo
choices.en: How about 2? Let's go after lunch
choices.feedback: Names a time and adds 점심 먹고 가요 — a small extra detail that makes the plan feel real, not just scheduled.

choices.en: I will see you at 2 PM.
choices.feedback: 뵙겠습니다 is honorific 합니다체 for a boss or a client, not for a classmate you study with.

choices.en: I don't eat breakfast.
choices.feedback: Grammatical but off-topic — they asked what time to meet.

turns.ko: 오케이! 그럼 이따 봐요
turns.romanization: okei! geureom itta bwayo
turns.en: Okay! See you later then

turns.prompt: Confirm and tell them to bring their notes.

choices.en: Sureㅋㅋ make sure you bring your notes
choices.feedback: 챙겨 와요 is a light 해요체 reminder — it closes the chat while giving them one useful thing to do.

choices.en: Please bring your notes.
choices.feedback: 지참해 주시기 바랍니다 belongs on an official notice board, not in a text to a classmate.

choices.en: By the way, how far does the exam go?
choices.feedback: A fine question at the wrong moment — they were saying bye, and this reopens the thread.

buddyCard.instructionKo: 같은 수업을 듣는 사람 역할을 해 주세요. 시험공부를 같이 하자는 제안을 받고, 어디서 몇 시에 만날지 해요체로 차례로 물어봐 주세요. 학습자는 초급이니 짧고 천천히 말해 주세요.

conversations.title: So what's new lately? (polite)
conversations.situation: An acquaintance you haven't seen in a while asks how you've been and what you've been up to.
conversations.tip: For the open-ended '요즘 뭐 해요?', give one small real detail and volley it back (요즘 어때요?). One-word answers in 해요체 sound polite but end the conversation.

turns.ko: 잘 지내요? 요즘 뭐 하고 지내요?
turns.romanization: jal jinaeyo? yojeum mwo hago jinaeyo?
turns.en: You doing well? What have you been up to lately?

turns.prompt: Say you're alright and give a tiny update, then ask back

choices.ko: 네 그냥 회사 다니죠 뭐ㅋㅋ 요즘 어떻게 지내요?
choices.romanization: ne geunyang hoesa danijyo mwokk yojeum eotteoke jinaeyo?
choices.en: Yeah, just working as usualㅋㅋ how have you been lately?
choices.feedback: ~죠 뭐 is a relaxed 해요체 shrug, and asking back keeps the check-in mutual rather than one-sided.

choices.ko: 덕분에 잘 지내고 있습니다. 귀하는 어떠신가요?
choices.romanization: deokbune jal jinaego itseumnida. gwihaneun eotteosingayo?
choices.en: I am doing well thanks to you. And how are you, sir?
choices.feedback: 귀하 is business-letter language. This is polite to the point of sounding like a form reply.

choices.en: What have you been up to lately?
choices.feedback: Bounces the question back without answering first — polite, but it reads as evasive.

turns.ko: 저요? 저 요즘 운동 시작했어요ㅋㅋ
turns.romanization: jeoyo? jeo yojeum undong sijakaesseoyokk
turns.en: Me? I started working out lately ㅋㅋ

turns.prompt: React with surprise and ask what kind

choices.en: Oh really? what kind? the gym?
choices.feedback: Reacting first (오 진짜요?) then asking a narrow follow-up shows you actually care — the engine of any check-in.

choices.en: Exercise is very beneficial for one's health.
choices.feedback: Textbook 합니다체. It responds to the topic but not to the person.

choices.en: Ah, I see.
choices.feedback: Polite but flat, with no follow-up. The conversation quietly dies here.

turns.ko: 네 헬스요ㅋㅋ 살 좀 빼려고요. 근데 너무 힘들어요
turns.romanization: ne helseuyokk sal jom ppaeryeogoyo. geunde neomu himdeureoyo
turns.en: Yeah, the gym ㅋㅋ trying to lose some weight. but it's so hard

turns.prompt: Sympathize and lightly relate

choices.ko: 헐 맞아요ㅋㅋ 저도 맨날 작심삼일이라 금방 포기해요
choices.romanization: heol majayokk jeodo maennal jaksimsamirira geumbang pogihaeyo
choices.en: Ugh, so trueㅋㅋ I always give up after a few days too.
choices.feedback: 헐 and 맞아요 agree naturally, and sharing your own version of the struggle makes it feel mutual, not just polite.

choices.ko: 체지방 감량을 위해서는 식단 관리가 필수입니다.
choices.romanization: chejibang gamnyangeul wihaeseoneun sikdan gwalliga pilsuimnida.
choices.en: Diet control is essential for reducing body fat.
choices.feedback: Reads like a fitness pamphlet — they wanted sympathy, not advice.

choices.en: Why are you trying to lose weight?
choices.feedback: Grammatical, but it's a prying question to an acquaintance and changes the mood.

turns.ko: ㅋㅋㅋ 그쵸 진짜. 우리 같이 운동할래요?
turns.romanization: kkk geuchyo jinjja. uri gachi undonghallaeyo?
turns.en: Lol right, for real. want to work out together?

turns.prompt: Show interest but stay realistic

choices.ko: 오 좋죠ㅋㅋ 근데 저 게을러서 끌고 가 주셔야 돼요
choices.romanization: o jochyokk geunde jeo geeulleoseo kkeulgo ga jusyeoya dwaeyo
choices.en: Oh, sounds greatㅋㅋ but I'm lazy, so you'll have to drag me along.
choices.feedback: A warm yes plus a self-deprecating joke. Humor works perfectly well in 해요체 and turns an acquaintance into a friend.

choices.en: I appreciate the offer but I must politely decline.
choices.feedback: Sounds like declining a business proposal — cold for someone just inviting you along.

choices.en: You're saying work out together?
choices.feedback: Repeats their question back instead of answering it, which stalls the invitation.

buddyCard.instructionKo: 오랜만에 만난 지인 역할을 해 주세요. 요즘 어떻게 지내는지와 새로 시작한 일이 있는지 해요체로 물어봐 주세요. 학습자는 초급이니 짧고 천천히 말해 주세요.

conversations.title: Long time, no text (polite)
conversations.situation: An acquaintance you haven't talked to in months suddenly texts you out of nowhere.
conversations.tip: When someone reaches out after a long gap, react first (헐/와 그러게요) and then bounce the same question back. In 해요체, the reaction is what keeps politeness from reading as distance.

turns.ko: 와 진짜 오랜만이에요ㅋㅋ
turns.romanization: wa jinjja oraenmanieyokk
turns.en: Wow, it's been forever ㅋㅋ

turns.prompt: React to how long it's been and toss it back

choices.en: Whoa, right?ㅋㅋ have you been doing okay?
choices.feedback: 그러게요 is the 해요체 맞장구 (matching reaction), and 잘 지냈어요? immediately gives them something to answer.

choices.en: Yes, thank you for reaching out after so long.
choices.feedback: Grammatical, but 감사합니다 for a text makes it sound like a client email. It quietly pushes them away.

choices.en: Yes.
choices.feedback: Polite and completely flat. No reaction, no question, no conversation.

turns.ko: 네 그럭저럭요? 갑자기 생각나서 연락했어요ㅋㅋ
turns.romanization: ne geureokjeoreogyo? gapjagi saenggangnaseo yeollakaesseoyokk
turns.en: Yeah, more or less? I just suddenly thought of you ㅋㅋ

turns.prompt: Say that's sweet and ask what made them think of you

choices.ko: 오 뭐예요ㅋㅋ 갑자기 왜 제 생각이 났어요?
choices.romanization: o mwoyeyokk gapjagi wae je saenggagi nasseoyo?
choices.en: Aw, what's this?ㅋㅋ what made you think of me all of a sudden?
choices.feedback: 뭐예요ㅋㅋ is playful, not rude, and asking 왜? digs into the warm thing they just said.

choices.en: I am honored that you thought of me.
choices.feedback: 영광입니다 is award-ceremony language. Nobody texts an acquaintance like this.

choices.en: I've been so-so too.
choices.feedback: Polite but it skips right past the nicest part of their message — that they thought of you.

turns.ko: 그냥 옛날 사진 보다가요ㅋㅋ 우리 그때 진짜 자주 봤는데요
turns.romanization: geunyang yennal sajin bodagayokk uri geuttae jinjja jaju bwanneundeyo
turns.en: Just looking at old pics ㅋㅋ we used to see each other so much back then

turns.prompt: Agree and admit you miss those days a little

choices.ko: 맞아요ㅋㅋ 그때 진짜 자주 만났는데요. 좀 그립네요, 그쵸?
choices.romanization: majayokk geuttae jinjja jaju mannanneundeyo. jom geurimneyo, geuchyo?
choices.en: Right?ㅋㅋ we did meet up all the time. I kind of miss it — you too?
choices.feedback: Agrees with the memory, then 그립네요, 그쵸? matches their nostalgic tone and invites them to say the same.

choices.en: Photos are personal data, so you should be careful.
choices.feedback: Technically polite advice, but it answers a warm memory with a warning. The mood dies instantly.

choices.en: Did we see each other a lot back then?
choices.feedback: Turning their line into a question sounds like you don't remember — a little cold here.

turns.ko: 맞아요 우리 조만간 한번 봐요 진짜
turns.romanization: majayo uri jomangan hanbeon bwayo jinjja
turns.en: Right, we should actually meet up sometime soon.

turns.prompt: Say yes and nudge toward actually setting it up

choices.ko: 좋아요ㅋㅋ 언제 시간 돼요? 날 잡아요
choices.romanization: joayokk eonje sigan dwaeyo? nal jabayo
choices.en: Sounds goodㅋㅋ when are you free? let's pick a day
choices.feedback: 언제 시간 돼요? and 날 잡아요 turn a vague 'someday' into a real plan — the whole point of the reconnect.

choices.en: I will review it positively.
choices.feedback: Corporate 합니다체 for meeting a person. It sounds like a polite no.

choices.en: Yeah, we'll meet someday I guess.
choices.feedback: Lukewarm — it brushes off their offer instead of taking them up on it.

buddyCard.instructionKo: 몇 달 만에 연락한 지인 역할을 해 주세요. 오랜만이라고 해요체로 인사하고, 그동안 잘 지냈는지 천천히 물어봐 주세요. 학습자는 초급이니 짧게 말해 주세요.

conversations.title: Congrats on the new job (polite)
conversations.situation: An acquaintance texts that they finally got hired after a long job hunt, and you celebrate with them.
conversations.tip: For big news, react big first (헐 대박!!! 축하해요) before asking anything. 해요체 does not mean toning the excitement down — acknowledging the grind (고생 많았어요) lands harder than a plain congrats.

turns.ko: 저 드디어 취뽀했어요!!!ㅠㅠㅠ
turns.romanization: jeo deudieo chwippohaesseoyo!!!yuyuyu
turns.en: I finally landed a job!!! ㅠㅠㅠ

turns.prompt: React big and congratulate them

choices.ko: 헐 대박!!! 진짜 축하해요ㅠㅠ 고생 많으셨어요
choices.romanization: heol daebak!!! jinjja chukahaeyoyuyu gosaeng maneusyeosseoyo
choices.en: Whoa, amazing!!! congrats for realㅠㅠ you worked so hard
choices.feedback: 헐 and 대박 are style-neutral, so they sit fine in 해요체, and 고생 많으셨어요 honors the long grind behind the news.

choices.en: I hereby sincerely congratulate you on your employment.
choices.feedback: 축하드리는 바입니다 is written, ceremonial language — it congratulates the news but not the person.

choices.en: Oh, which company?
choices.feedback: Polite, but jumping straight to questions without celebrating first feels cold for news this big.

turns.ko: ㅠㅠ 진짜 면접을 몇 번이나 봤는지 몰라요. 너무 오래 걸렸어요
turns.romanization: yuyu jinjja myeonjeobeul myeot beonina bwanneunji mollayo. neomu orae geollyeosseoyo
turns.en: ㅠㅠ I lost count of how many interviews I had. It took so long.

turns.prompt: Acknowledge how hard it was and ask which company

choices.ko: ㅠㅠ 그쵸 그쵸 진짜 고생 많았어요 어느 회사예요??
choices.romanization: yuyu geuchyo geuchyo jinjja gosaeng manasseoyo eoneu hoesayeyo??
choices.en: ㅠㅠ I know, I know, you really went through a lot — which company is it??
choices.feedback: Empathize first (고생 많았어요), then ask the follow-up they're waiting to answer. That order is what keeps it flowing.

choices.ko: 구직 활동의 노고를 충분히 이해하는 바입니다.
choices.romanization: guji kwaldongui nogoreul chungbunhi ihaehaneun baimnida.
choices.en: I fully understand the toils of your job-seeking efforts.
choices.feedback: 노고 and 이해하는 바입니다 belong in a speech. It sounds like a statement, not sympathy.

choices.en: You did that many interviews?
choices.feedback: Repeats their line back as a question instead of reacting to it — the emotion goes unanswered.

turns.ko: 그 아이티 회사요! 저 다음 달부터 출근이에요ㅋㅋㅋ
turns.romanization: geu aiti hoesayo! jeo daeum dalbuteo chulgeunieyokkk
turns.en: That IT company! I start next month ㅋㅋ

turns.prompt: React and tease them lightly about a celebration

choices.ko: 와 진짜 대박이에요ㅋㅋ 이건 한턱 쏘셔야 되는 거 알죠?
choices.romanization: wa jinjja daebagieyokk igeon hanteok ssosyeoya doeneun geo aljyo?
choices.en: Wow, that's amazingㅋㅋ you know you have to treat me, right?
choices.feedback: 알죠? is teasing in 해요체 — the light 한턱 쏘다 joke is exactly how people celebrate good news without getting stiff.

choices.ko: 입사 후 첫 급여일에 식사를 제공해 주시기 바랍니다.
choices.romanization: ipsa hu cheot geubyeoire siksareul jegonghae jusigi baramnida.
choices.en: Please provide a meal on your first payday after joining.
choices.feedback: Reads like a formal request memo. The joke is there, but the register kills it.

choices.en: I heard IT companies have a lot of overtime.
choices.feedback: Negative and off-topic — it deflates the happy news instead of celebrating it.

turns.ko: ㅋㅋㅋ 당연하죠 제가 거하게 쏠게요 뭐 먹고 싶어요?
turns.romanization: kkk dangyeonhajyo jega geohage ssolgeyo mwo meokgo sipeoyo?
turns.en: Lol of course, I'll treat you big time — what do you want to eat?

turns.prompt: Happily accept and suggest meeting up to celebrate

choices.ko: 오예ㅋㅋ 그럼 이번 주말에 만나서 제대로 축하해요!
choices.romanization: oyekk geureom ibeon jumare mannaseo jedaero chukahaeyo!
choices.en: Yesssㅋㅋ let's meet this weekend and celebrate properly then!
choices.feedback: An excited yes plus ~해요 as a suggestion turns the chat into an actual plan — the strongest way to close.

choices.ko: 메뉴 및 일정은 별도 협의 후 확정하겠습니다.
choices.romanization: menyu mit iljeongeun byeoldo hyeobui hu hwakjeonghagetseumnida.
choices.en: The menu and schedule will be finalized after separate consultation.
choices.feedback: Meeting-minutes language. It answers the question but sounds like scheduling a vendor call.

choices.en: You really worked so hard.
choices.feedback: Kind, but you already said this — repeating it ignores their offer and lets the chat stall.

buddyCard.instructionKo: 오랜 구직 끝에 취업한 지인 역할을 해 주세요. 취업 소식을 해요체로 천천히 전하고, 만나서 무엇을 먹으며 축하할지 물어봐 주세요. 학습자는 초급이니 짧게 말해 주세요.
